get.summary: Every market on one race: win, place, Top 2/3/4 and exotic dividends
get.description:
Cost: 2 credits. One race, every market the panel quotes on it, book by book: the win
price, the place price, the Same Race Multi legs (**Top 2, Top 3 and Top 4**), each book's
market percentage, the best price per runner in each market, and — once the race has been
run — the exotic dividends it paid.

**Naming the race.** `race_id` is exact. Failing that, `venue` + `meeting_date` (the AET
meeting date) + `race_number`, with `country` when two meetings share the name on one
date (Ascot in Perth and in Berkshire on 2026-10-17) and `category` when two codes race
under one name (Sale on 2026-10-25, horses and greyhounds); two races still sharing those
answer 409 `race_ambiguous`, naming each with its code and country, and cost nothing,
because picking one of a venue split silently would be worse than refusing. ONE race listed
under several race_ids is not a split (since 2026-10-28): a delayed meeting keeps a row at
the old start beside the new one while the books move across (Morphettville on 2026-10-24,
every race), and the race most books price is served, with the others in `twin_race_ids`.

**Who quotes what.** Every book in the panel prices win, and all but the exchange price
place. Top 2/3/4 come from **sportsbet, ladbrokes_au, neds and pointsbetau** — no other
book in the feed publishes Same Race Multi legs, so an empty `top3` is a fact about the
market and not a gap in the feed. Each leg is validated against the chain
win >= top2 >= top3 >= top4 > 1.0 before it is stored, so a leg that would break it is
absent rather than wrong.

**overround_pct** is Σ (1/price) × 100 over the runners that book quoted in that market —
100% is a book taking no margin. It is null where a book quoted fewer than two runners,
which is not a market. Place and Top-N percentages are naturally far above 100 because
several runners can win the bet.

**Live or stored.** A race whose market is still open is read live (`source: "live"`). Once
it has been run the live rows are purged, and the answer comes from the minute-by-minute
capture of the last price each book showed before the jump (`source: "closes"`). Races that
jumped before that capture began carry no market rows and say so in `note`.

**exotics** are SETTLED DIVIDENDS — what the tote paid — not prices. Nothing in this feed
quotes fixed-odds quinella, exacta, trifecta or first four before a race, so `exotics` is
null until the race is resulted, and then carries the result's own `status`: `interim`
dividends can still move, `final` cannot.

**quote_detail** (since 2026-09-29) lists, per book and runner, what the book publishes
beside its prices: `open_price` (the book's own opening price — not the archive's first
captured price), `flucs` (its recent prices, most recent first), `tote_win` / `tote_place`
(its tote dividends keyed by product code; `PROV` is an indicative pre-race dividend that
moves until the pool closes), `boost_price` / `boost_type`, and the exchange fields. Each
entry names `bookmaker`, `number`, `name`, `runner_ref` and `seen_at` — when the book was
last read — and only the fields that book carries. Who carries them, measured on the AU
board of 2026-09-29 before its first race (20 races, 2,219 book-runner rows): flucs at
betdeluxe, betgold, boostbet and betright on every row, open_price at betright on every
row, tote_win at tabtouch on 89 of 194 rows and tote_place on 26 (a provisional dividend
appears as the pool forms), no boost that morning. The exchange fields are Betfair's, and
Betfair is withheld from customer answers. For a race that has been run the values are
the last read before the jump.

**scratchings** (since 2026-09-29) are the race's scratched runners — `name`, `number`,
`barrier`, `scratched_at` (the scratching book's own time, UTC) and `vacant` for an empty
box — from the open race while it is live, and once it has been purged from the capture
taken at the jump. A race run before 2026-09-29 answers an empty list after its purge. A
scratching no Australian bookmaker has reported, while two or more of them still price the
runner, is held back: the runner stays in the markets until a bookmaker reports it.

**tote_series** (since 2026-10-06) is each book's tote approximate as the pools formed:
one entry per book and runner, with points at fixed marks before the jump — 3600, 1800,
900, 600, 300, 180, 120 and 60 seconds — each the first read the minute-by-minute capture
saw at or inside its mark, carrying `mark_seconds`, `read_at`, `secs_to_jump` and
`tote_win` / `tote_place` by product code. TABtouch publishes a provisional dividend
(`PROV`) for every runner hours out; BetRight its products in the final quarter hour. A
race first seen inside a mark has no earlier points: nothing is filled in. The last read
before the jump stays in `quote_detail`.

**book_scratchings** (since 2026-10-06) says, book by book, when a scratching reached each
feed: `reported_at` is the first time that book's own feed listed it, `book_scratched_at`
the scratch time the book itself states (Ladbrokes, Neds, BetRight and the BetMakers books
carry one), and `first_quoted_at` / `last_quoted_at` with `last_quoted_win` the polls, to
the minute, at which that book's feed still carried a win price for the runner after the
race's scratchings named it. Ladbrokes and Neds keep a scratched runner's last price on the
card beside their own flag, so for a book that flags it the price is recorded once, at the
flag: its price at the scratching. A book that carries a price with no flag is recorded
each minute until it clears the runner. None of these prices is served as a price: a
scratched runner is dropped from every price endpoint.

**Your own links** (`source_link` beside each runner's `source_url`, since 2026-10-14, Plus
and above): store your bookmaker link templates once with `PUT /v1/link-templates` and each
price also carries a ready-made link built through them. Absent where there is nothing to
link, and for an account with no stored templates.

Plus and above, and Standard keys issued before 20 September 2026. Every other key below
Plus receives a 403 and is not charged; the 403 carries a `sample`: the winner of one
recent race, its best price in each market and the book that offered it.

get.summary: The market consensus on one race: margin-free probability per runner
get.description:
Cost: 3 credits. The market's consensus on one race while its market is open: for
every runner, the implied probability after each book's margin is removed and the books
are combined, the price that probability corresponds to, the median, mean, best and
worst price, and how far the best available price sits from the consensus. The inputs
are printed beside the answer — which books were counted, which were left out and why.

**Naming the race.** `race_id` from /v1/racing/next-to-go or /v1/racing/events is exact.
Failing that, `venue` + `meeting_date` (the AET meeting date) + `race_number`, with
`country` when two meetings share the name on one date (Ascot in Perth and in Berkshire
on 2026-10-17) and `category` when two codes race under one name (Sale on 2026-10-25);
two races still sharing those answer 409 `race_ambiguous`, naming each with its code, and
cost nothing. One race listed under several race_ids during a delay is served, not refused
(since 2026-10-28): the race most books price, its other ids in `twin_race_ids`.

**How the number is made.** Each included book's win prices on the field are turned into
implied probabilities (1 / price) and its margin removed — `power` (default) raises them
to the exponent that makes them sum to one, at most 1.25 (a book that needs more, usually
one with a very short favourite, has the rest divided out in proportion), and
`multiplicative` divides them by their sum — so every book contributes a field that sums
to 1. The consensus for a runner is the
MEDIAN of those per-book probabilities, and the medians are scaled once so the field
sums to 1 again; `market.consensus_sum_before_normalisation` shows how far from 1 they
were before scaling. Every included book counts once. Nothing is weighted by an opinion
of which book is sharp.

**Which books count.** A book is included when it is visible to you (the exchange and the
non-Australian reference books are withheld here as on every racing endpoint), its quote
is inside its refresh-tier threshold (the same per-book rule next-to-go publishes: 120 s
inside three hours of the jump, 1800 s on the morning card, with Betr and NextBet on
their own horizons), and it prices the complete field — `market.field_size` is the number
of runners a complete-field book quotes, and a book pricing fewer is `partial_field`.
Placeholder prices are dropped quote by quote on the rule /v1/racing/best-odds applies
(a long price at least four times the median of three or more other books) and listed in
`excluded_quotes`. Scratched runners are dropped and listed under `scratchings`.

**Reading `consensus_prob`.** It is the market's implied probability after margin, not a
probability of winning and not a fair price. `best_vs_consensus_pct` is
best_price / consensus_price − 1: negative is normal, because every quoted price carries
margin and the best quote usually sits below the panel's margin-free price (about −20 %
on a 130 % greyhound market); it turns positive only when one book prices a runner above
the panel's margin-free view. It says where the best quote sits, nothing more. The
fields a reader would use to judge how much to trust a figure — `books`, the spread, the
ages, `secs_to_jump` — are separate on purpose; there is no single confidence score.

**Live only.** The consensus is read from the open market. A race that has left the live
board answers 404; the consensus at the close will arrive as columns on the permanent
archive, where it belongs. A race inside the ten minutes after its jump is still served
(`status: jumped`) while the books drop off, with a note.

Every plan, Free included. 3 credits, charged after the race is found; a race we cannot
find, an unparseable parameter and an unknown bookmaker key are free.

get.summary: Market intelligence on one race: consensus at fixed marks, time-anchored moves, breadth, first mover, signal
get.description:
Cost: 3 credits. One race on the live board: for every runner, the market consensus
price now and at fixed marks before the jump (T-60, T-30, T-15, T-10, T-5, T-2), its high
and low since capture began, movement measured against those marks and against the last
five and two minutes, the number of ticks in the last five minutes, the best price against
the consensus, how many books moved with the headline, the first attributable book to move,
and a signal class whose rule is printed in the response.

**Naming the race.** `race_id` from /v1/racing/next-to-go or /v1/racing/events is exact.
Failing that, `venue` + `meeting_date` (AET) + `race_number`, with `country` when two
meetings share the name on one date and `category` when two codes race under one name; a
venue split answers 409, naming each race and its code, and costs nothing. One race listed
under several race_ids during a delay is served, not refused (since 2026-10-28): the race
most books price, its other ids in `twin_race_ids`.

**Time-anchored, not open-anchored.** Every movement figure compares the consensus NOW with
the consensus at a fixed time, computed by the same arithmetic as GET /v1/racing/consensus
and the archive's consensus columns: each book's win prices with its margin removed, the
median across books, the field scaled to one. `move_from_t60_pct` is negative for a runner
that shortened. A mark is null when the race had not entered the capture window by then —
capture begins 60 minutes before the jump, so a race further out than that carries `now`
only and `window.open` is false.

**Breadth.** `with_history` counts books quoting now with two or more captured prices on
the runner; `firming`, `drifting` and `unchanged` partition them by each book's own price
against its price at T-60 (or its first tick, when it joined later). A headline move that
most of `with_history` did not make is one book repricing, not the market.

**First mover** names the earliest attributable book to move at least 5 % in the headline
direction, with its lead over the next book and the median lag of the followers. It is
`undetermined` when fewer than two attributable books moved or when the lead is inside the
30-second attribution floor (the books are polled every 8–17 seconds). Books whose
timestamps cannot order a move are excluded and named in `method`: push-fed books (the stamp
is the receipt, not the read) and books polled slower than the floor.

**Signal** is one of `strong_firm`, `firm`, `steady`, `drift`, `strong_drift` or
`insufficient`, from `move_from_t60_pct` and the breadth, by the rule in `method.signal_rule`.
It is a classification of what the market did, not a prediction; its strike rate against
results will be published on the market report once the archive carries it.

**Live only.** A race that has left the live board answers 404; a race inside the ten
minutes after its jump is still served while the books drop off, with a note.

Every plan, Free included. 3 credits, charged after the race is found.

get.description:
Cost: 5 credits. Every race inside the 60-minute capture window, analysed exactly as
GET /v1/racing/intelligence analyses one race, with the runners that cleared the filters
returned largest move first. This is the time-anchored, breadth-gated form of
/v1/racing/movers, and /movers keeps serving unchanged.

`window` selects the movement figure the gate applies to: `60m` for the move since the
T-60 consensus, `15m` since T-15, `5m` over the last five minutes — the late-window
figure a last-minute mover product wants. `min_books` is the breadth gate: a runner needs
that many books with two or more captured prices, so a single book repricing cannot clear
it. `signal` keeps only the named classes. The response carries the race header beside
each runner so nothing has to be joined.

Served from a 15-second cache shared by every caller with the same filters; `cached`
says so and `as_of` is the moment the scan was computed.

get.summary: The market's path per runner, stored at the jump: consensus at fixed marks, moves, breadth, first mover, signal
get.description:
Cost: 5 credits (JSON) / 20 credits (CSV). The market summary archive: one row per race
and runner, written at the jump, carrying the market consensus price at T-60, T-30, T-15,
T-10, T-5 and T-2 and at the close, its high and low through the capture window,
`move_from_t60_pct` / `move_from_t15_pct` / `move_t5_close_pct` (close against those
marks; negative is a runner that shortened), the breadth of the move (books with history,
firming, drifting, unchanged), the first attributable book to move with its lead and the
followers' median lag, the signal class, and the best closing price against the consensus.

**It is GET /v1/racing/intelligence, kept.** The same analysis, run at the jump with the
archive's own `consensus_close_price` as the close (`close_source: archive`; a runner the
archive could not score falls back to the ticks at the jump, `close_source: ticks`), so a
live reading and the stored row are one quantity. The ticks it is built from live in the
45-day snapshot store; this row is permanent, from `summary_from` forward.

**Joined at serve time, appended last:** `venue_id`, `venue_site`, `horse_ref`, and the
runner's `finish_position` and `result_status` from the closing-line archive, which land
after the summary is written. Scratched runners carry no row.

**The signal classes against results** are what this table exists for. `signal` filters
on them; joined to `finish_position` the table says, for any window, how often each class
won and at what price. Those strike rates belong on the market report; until they are
printed there, compute them from this table rather than trusting the label.

**Plans.** Plus and above read the whole table; Standard a rolling 90-day window
(`window_days` 90, `X-Archive-Window-Days`); Free and Hobby a free 403. Standard keys
issued before 2026-09-20 keep the whole archive they were sold. `date=` is a single-day
alias for `from`/`to`; an unknown parameter, signal or date is a free 422.

put.description:
Cost: 0 credits. Store how every bookmaker link in your racing responses should be built.
A FULL replacement: send the whole document each time.

Once stored, every racing response that carries a bookmaker URL also carries a ready-made
twin built through your templates: `source_link` beside `source_url` (next-to-go legs,
best-odds quotes, markets), `betslip_win_link` / `betslip_place_link` beside the betslip
URLs (next-to-go, changes) and `betslip_link` beside `betslip_url` (best-odds). Put the
`*_link` value on your page. A twin is absent where there is nothing to link: the book gave
no URL, or your rule for that book is "none". The `*_url` fields are unchanged.

The document:

- `mode`: what a book without its own rule gets. `"source"` (default) links straight to the
  bookmaker's URL, `"template"` sends it through `template`, `"none"` gives no link.
- `template`: your tracking link with `{url}` where the bookmaker's URL goes
  (percent-encoded), or `{url_raw}` to insert it unencoded. Must start `https://`. Required
  when `mode` is `"template"`.
- `per_bookmaker`: a rule per bookmaker key (`ladbrokes_au`, `unibet`, `tab`, ...): a
  template, `"source"` or `"none"`. It beats `mode`. An unknown key is refused, so a typo
  cannot silently drop a book's link.

We append nothing of our own to any link. Whether a bookmaker's affiliate programme credits
a click, and whether it accepts a deep-link destination at all, is between you and that
programme. Prices shown to your users still need the visible "Prices by PuntersEdge"
credit your plan's licence requires (Terms 8.1 and 8.3); Platform's white-label widget is
the version without it.

Takes effect on your next request. Primary key only. Step-by-step guide with curl, Python and
JavaScript examples: https://puntersedge.online/developers/affiliate-links

date_status.title: Date Status
date_status.description: 'past', 'today' or 'future', relative to the Australia/Sydney date. On 'past' this card is a FROZEN SNAPSHOT: acceptances are collected for today and forward only, so a meeting still showing acceptances_published false will never fill in and the scratching set can never converge. On 'today'/'future' the next collection pass CAN add acceptances and scratchings, every two hours — but that is not a promise that a meeting converges. Racing Australia stops listing a meeting once it is UNDERWAY, so a meeting's rows stop advancing around 12:15-14:15 AEST while its own races are still running to 17:00-19:30. Log-verified 2026-09-09: the 02:15Z pass discovered all six of that day's meetings, the 04:15Z pass discovered one, the 06:15Z pass discovered none. The in-band signal is per meeting, not per day — watch its own as_of and scratching_sheet_as_of: a stamp that stops moving while later passes land on other meetings is a meeting that has gone underway, not a quiet one. From that point race-day movement is on /v1/racing/changes, not here.

runner_count.title: Runner Count
runner_count.description: Acceptance rows on this card — scratched runners and emergencies INCLUDED. A floor, not a guarantee, wherever a race reports runner_set_status other than 'checks_passed'.

emergency_count.title: Emergency Count
emergency_count.description: Rows flagged as an emergency acceptance. NULL unless every meeting with rows on this card has emergency_data 'parsed' — see completeness. A FLOOR, not an exact figure, wherever a race reports runner_set_status other than 'checks_passed': it counts only the acceptance rows this card holds.

declared_count.title: Declared Count
declared_count.description: runner_count minus emergency_count: the DECLARED field, i.e. the acceptances that are not emergencies. NULL when emergency_count is. A FLOOR wherever a race reports runner_set_status other than 'checks_passed'.

scratched_count.title: Scratched Count
scratched_count.description: Sheet rows MATCHED to an acceptance row this card holds — NOT every scratching Racing Australia lists. A sheet row with no acceptance row here is not counted; it appears in that race's missing_runners with scratched true. Measured 2026-09-08: Townsville R6 has scratching_data 'parsed' and scratched_count 0 while the sheet holds #4 Five Star King and #9 Kickoff, so the true figure is at least 2. Read it as a FLOOR wherever a race reports runner_set_status other than 'checks_passed'; that race's runner_set_note states the bound. NULL unless every meeting with rows on this card has scratching_data 'parsed' — a meeting with no sheet cannot be said to have nobody scratched.

unscratched_count.title: Unscratched Count
unscratched_count.description: runner_count minus scratched_count. A RECONCILIATION number against the sheet, NOT a field size: it still includes emergencies, which run only if promoted. A FLOOR wherever a race reports runner_set_status other than 'checks_passed'. NULL when scratched_count is.

declared_scratched_count.title: Declared Scratched Count
declared_scratched_count.description: Rows that are scratched AND not emergencies. Like scratched_count it counts only sheet rows MATCHED to an acceptance row held here, so it is a FLOOR wherever a race reports runner_set_status other than 'checks_passed'. NULL unless BOTH emergency_data and scratching_data are 'parsed' for every meeting with rows.

declared_remaining_count.title: Declared Remaining Count
declared_remaining_count.description: declared_count minus declared_scratched_count: the horses expected to jump barring an emergency promotion, which Racing Australia does not publish. It is the number to render as the field ONLY where every race behind it reports runner_set_status 'checks_passed'. Anywhere else it is a FLOOR — render it as 'at least N', never as an exact field: a runner Racing Australia lists that this card does not hold, and that is not on the scratching sheet, may well be jumping. Measured 2026-09-08: Townsville R5 is 'gap_detected' with saddlecloth #6 unaccounted for and published 11. The race's runner_set_note states the bound. NULL unless BOTH facts are known everywhere.

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: Newest RA scrape backing the meetings actually returned, UTC — computed after the venue filter.

coverage_from.title: Coverage From
coverage_from.description: The first meeting day (Australia/Sydney) this store holds an acceptance card for, read from the tables on every call — never a constant. Every day from here up to three days ahead is served; an earlier `date` is a free 422 naming this same day. Until 2026-09-29 the reference tables were deleted three days after each meeting, so the store begins at the oldest day that survived that (2026-09-26) and grows by one day per day. Null only when the store could not be read, and then the older 3-day rule applies.

backtest_ready_rows.description: Rows that pass the recommended modelling filter: is_closing_line AND NOT scratched AND NOT venue_split_suspect AND NOT name_fragment_suspect AND NOT duplicate_suspect (an absent flag counts as false). Added 2026-10-19.

One row per period: {period, from|to, rows, closing_rows, closing_pct, basis}. Added 2026-10-19.

finish_position_pct.description: Of the rows whose race has a result, excluding runners the result marked scratched, the share carrying a finish_position. Books differ widely, so filter on the flags rather than trusting the aggregate.

settleable_races_in_window.title: Settleable Races In Window
settleable_races_in_window.description: AU and NZ archive races in the window that started at least 3 hours ago (the denominator of races_without_result).

races_result_unlinked.title: Races Result Unlinked
races_result_unlinked.description: Of races_without_result, races whose result exists under a different race_id (category, a start within two minutes and the venue's first word match). Added 2026-10-19.

results_in_window.title: Results In Window
results_in_window.description: AU and NZ results in the window that started at least 3 hours ago (the denominator of results_without_race).

results_without_race.title: Results Without Race
results_without_race.description: Of results_in_window, results with no archive race (no closing line at any served book).

definitions.title: Definitions
definitions.description: One line per gap and rate above, saying exactly what is counted.

credits_blocked.title: Credits Blocked
credits_blocked.description: True when your remaining credits are below the cost of one horse, which pauses collection until they reset or you upgrade.

queue_position.title: Queue Position
queue_position.description: Horses ahead of this job's oldest waiting row, across all jobs.

ready_to_collect.title: Ready To Collect
ready_to_collect.description: Completed rows you have not yet read.

upstream.description: Whether Racing Australia is answering form reads at all. Added 2026-09-21 and purely additive: nothing else on this response, and nothing about billing or the queue, changed with it.

horses.title: Horses
horses.description: Horse names, `pe:` horse_refs or `ra:` entry codes, in any mix. Max 500 per call. A name and its horse_ref resolve identically, against acceptances and archived results; an `ra:` code pins one meeting's entry.

label.title: Label
label.description: Your own tag for this batch, echoed back on status.

queued.title: Queued
queued.description: Horses accepted and waiting on the worker.

already_stored.title: Already Stored
already_stored.description: Horses we already hold a fresh copy of — matched on the HORSE, so a page collected under any of its Racing Australia codes counts. Collectable immediately, still billed at 3 credits each.

duplicates.title: Duplicates
duplicates.description: Already queued for you; not queued twice.

not_found.title: Not Found
not_found.description: Names we have never seen on our own feeds.

ambiguous.title: Ambiguous
ambiguous.description: Names matching several horses. Re-submit with the runner_ref you meant.

estimated_ready.title: Estimated Ready
estimated_ready.description: UTC estimate for the last horse, from the worker's measured pace.

schema_version.title: Schema Version
schema_version.description: Bumped whenever the dataset's columns change. Compare it with the value your loader was written against.

dataset_version.title: Dataset Version
dataset_version.description: Date of the last change to the rules that decide this dataset's rows or values. Files generated before that date were made under the earlier rules.

source_notes.title: Source Notes
source_notes.description: What is withheld, quarantined or flagged in this dataset, and why.

columns.title: Columns
columns.description: Column order of every file in this dataset, read from the newest file's sidecar.

days.title: Days
days.description: Daily files, oldest first. Business and above.

months.title: Months
months.description: Monthly bundles, oldest first. Platform and above.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: day (YYYY-MM-DD, Sydney meeting date) or month (YYYY-MM).

sha256.title: Sha256
sha256.description: Digest per format; also the ETag.

schema_version.title: Schema Version
schema_version.description: The column-set version this file was written under. Null on files written before versioning began (2026-10-13).

dataset_version.title: Dataset Version
dataset_version.description: The rules date this file was written under (see the dataset's dataset_version).

restatements.title: Restatements
restatements.description: How many times this file has changed after it was first published; /v1/bulk/restatements lists each one with its reason.

race_id.title: Race Id
race_id.description: Stable race identifier — the same id /v1/racing/next-to-go, /v1/racing/price-history and /v1/racing/results use.

country.title: Country
country.description: ISO country code, or null while the meeting is unresolved.

start_time.title: Start Time
start_time.description: Advertised start, UTC. It is revised as the meeting firms, and a revision bumps this race into the feed.

status.title: Status
status.description: Set when the race row is created and revised exactly once, if at all: to 'abandoned' when Racing Australia posts an official abandoned, postponed or transferred notice for the meeting — that revision bumps every runner of the race into this feed (2026-09-06). Otherwise it reads 'open' for every race here. It is not a live market-state signal — do not poll this endpoint for it.

market_status.title: Market Status
market_status.description: Betting-market state (OPEN, SUSPENDED, CLOSED). Reported by PointsBet, which sends CLOSED when it shuts its book at the jump, and by the Betfair Exchange, which is withheld from customer responses pending a data licence — so a value last written by the exchange reads null for customers. Same shape as /v1/racing/events.

inplay.title: Inplay
inplay.description: True once the market is in-play. Exchange-only — bookmakers do not run racing in-play — so it carries the same licence hold as `market_status` and reads null for customers.

market_closed_at.title: Market Closed At
market_closed_at.description: UTC time the market was FIRST seen shut. Poll-observed and set once — see /v1/racing/events for the full semantics. Served when a BOOKMAKER reported the transition; null for customers when the exchange was the only feed that saw it. Null never means the market stayed open.

inplay_at.title: Inplay At
inplay_at.description: UTC time the race was FIRST seen in-play — the actual off, as opposed to `start_time`, which is advertised and moves. Exchange-only, so null for customer plans.

market_state_source.title: Market State Source
market_state_source.description: Which feed's market state produced `market_closed_at` / `inplay_at` — 'pointsbetau' or 'betfair_ex_au'. Set once, with the first stamp, and null whenever those stamps are withheld.

scratchings.title: Scratchings
scratchings.description: The COMPLETE current scratchings for this race, merged across every book that reports one — not a delta, so a runner leaving the list is visible as an absence. Greyhound cards also carry box-vacancy placeholders here (a literal '....' or 'Vacant Box'), which name an empty box rather than a withdrawn runner; match on `number` and treat a name from that set as a vacant box.

track_condition_changed_at.title: Track Condition Changed At
track_condition_changed_at.description: UTC instant of the most recent logged track-condition, weather or rail transition for this race's meeting (2026-09-05). Null when nothing has changed since we began watching it. Read it with `track_condition`: the value says WHAT, this says WHEN.

track_condition.title: Track Condition
track_condition.description: The race's CURRENT track condition, not a change log — a poller diffing against what it holds sees a condition change the same way it sees a scratching. Null where no source reports it.

weather.title: Weather
weather.description: Current weather for the meeting, same read-as-current rule as track_condition.

changed_runners.title: Changed Runners
changed_runners.description: Runner prices that moved inside the window. An empty list means this race arrived on the race-level arm alone — expected, and explained in the endpoint description.

name.title: Name
name.description: Runner name as the bookmaker publishes it.

number.title: Number
number.description: Saddlecloth / rug number, where the book supplies one.

win_price.title: Win Price
win_price.description: Current fixed win price at this bookmaker.

place_price.title: Place Price
place_price.description: Current fixed place price. A place-only move does not advance `updated_at` — see the endpoint description.

top2_price.title: Top2 Price
top2_price.description: Current Top 2 (first-two) price at this bookmaker, where quoted.

top3_price.title: Top3 Price
top3_price.description: Current Top 3 price at this bookmaker, where quoted.

top4_price.title: Top4 Price
top4_price.description: Current Top 4 price at this bookmaker, where quoted.

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: UTC instant this runner's win or lay price last CHANGED at this bookmaker. Not the last poll: ingest carries this timestamp forward while the price is steady.

betslip_win_url.title: Betslip Win Url
betslip_win_url.description: Opens this bookmaker's betslip with this runner's fixed WIN selected. Plus and above. Present only for the books with a runner-level route (unibet, tab, ladbrokes_au, neds) — see /v1/racing/next-to-go for the per-book table and the daily check behind it.

betslip_place_url.title: Betslip Place Url
betslip_place_url.description: Same, fixed PLACE. Null when the book has a win link but is not quoting the place; on TAB it is the same one-shot URL as the win link.

betslip_app_only.title: Betslip App Only
betslip_app_only.description: True for Ladbrokes and Neds: those URLs open the native app and redirect to the app-download page in a desktop browser.

betslip_win_link.title: Betslip Win Link
betslip_win_link.description: Your own link for betslip_win_url, built through the link templates stored with PUT /v1/link-templates. Absent when your account stores none, or there is nothing to link.

betslip_place_link.title: Betslip Place Link
betslip_place_link.description: Your own link for betslip_place_url, built the same way. Absent when there is nothing to link.

race_id.title: Race Id
race_id.description: Race id; joins /v1/racing/results and /v1/racing/markets. Never null.

start_time.title: Start Time
start_time.description: Advertised start, UTC, ISO 8601 with Z. Never null.

meeting_date_aet.title: Meeting Date Aet
meeting_date_aet.description: Meeting date, YYYY-MM-DD, Australian Eastern calendar. Never null.

venue.title: Venue
venue.description: Venue name as the books list it. Never null.

runner_key.title: Runner Key
runner_key.description: Normalised runner name; the runner's key within the race. Never null.

runner_name.title: Runner Name
runner_name.description: Runner name as published. Never null.

open_win_price.title: Open Win Price
open_win_price.description: Win price at the first observation of the series.

open_secs_to_jump.title: Open Secs To Jump
open_secs_to_jump.description: Seconds to the jump at the first observation.

open_is_baseline.title: Open Is Baseline
open_is_baseline.description: FLAG. True when the series began at the 60-minute window entry, so open_win_price is a market open; false when the book joined mid-window. Never null.

close_win_price.title: Close Win Price
close_win_price.description: Win price at the last observation before the jump.

close_lay_price.title: Close Lay Price
close_lay_price.description: Exchange lay price at the close; null for customers (exchange rows are withheld).

close_secs_to_jump.title: Close Secs To Jump
close_secs_to_jump.description: Seconds to the jump at the last observation.

is_closing_line.title: Is Closing Line
is_closing_line.description: FLAG. True when the last observation was within 300 seconds of the jump: a genuine closing line. False rows carry a last-seen price. Never null.

points_observed.title: Points Observed
points_observed.description: Price points in the series. Never null.

finish_position.title: Finish Position
finish_position.description: Finishing position where the result publishes one. Null does NOT mean the runner lost; read result_status.

result_status.title: Result Status
result_status.description: The race's result status; null when the race has no result.

venue_split_suspect.title: Venue Split Suspect
venue_split_suspect.description: FLAG. The row may belong to a race the feed split across two venue spellings. Excluded by default. Never null.

venue_split_peer_race_id.title: Venue Split Peer Race Id
venue_split_peer_race_id.description: FLAG companion. The other race_id of a suspected venue split.

name_fragment_suspect.title: Name Fragment Suspect
name_fragment_suspect.description: FLAG. The runner name looks like a fragment of another runner's name. Excluded by default. Never null.

venue_id.title: Venue Id
venue_id.description: Canonical venue id from the venue registry.

venue_site.title: Venue Site
venue_site.description: Canonical venue site from the venue registry.

runner_ref.title: Runner Ref
runner_ref.description: Registry id for the runner on race day (ra:, grv:, grsa:).

horse_ref.title: Horse Ref
horse_ref.description: Horse identity across meetings (pe:<name>); thoroughbreds only.

scratched.title: Scratched
scratched.description: FLAG. The result marked this runner scratched, yet a book kept pricing it. Excluded by default. On harness and NZ rows false means not known. Never null.

open_place_price.title: Open Place Price
open_place_price.description: Place price at the first observation (from 2026-09-29).

close_place_price.title: Close Place Price
close_place_price.description: Place price at the last observation (from 2026-09-29).

scratched_at.title: Scratched At
scratched_at.description: When the runner was scratched, UTC, as the board stamped it (from 2026-09-29).

open_top2_price.title: Open Top2 Price
open_top2_price.description: Same Race Multi Top 2 price at the first observation.

open_top3_price.title: Open Top3 Price
open_top3_price.description: Same Race Multi Top 3 price at the first observation.

open_top4_price.title: Open Top4 Price
open_top4_price.description: Same Race Multi Top 4 price at the first observation.

close_top2_price.title: Close Top2 Price
close_top2_price.description: Same Race Multi Top 2 price at the last observation.

close_top3_price.title: Close Top3 Price
close_top3_price.description: Same Race Multi Top 3 price at the last observation.

close_top4_price.title: Close Top4 Price
close_top4_price.description: Same Race Multi Top 4 price at the last observation.

consensus_close_prob.title: Consensus Close Prob
consensus_close_prob.description: Market consensus probability at the close, margin removed.

books_in_consensus_close.title: Books In Consensus Close
books_in_consensus_close.description: Books the closing consensus rests on.

books_in_consensus_open.title: Books In Consensus Open
books_in_consensus_open.description: Books the opening consensus rests on.

duplicate_suspect.title: Duplicate Suspect
duplicate_suspect.description: FLAG. The row's race appears to duplicate another race record (the same race filed twice); duplicate_of_race_id names the other. The key is absent until the archive carries the flag.

duplicate_of_race_id.title: Duplicate Of Race Id
duplicate_of_race_id.description: FLAG companion. The race_id this row's race duplicates. Absent until the archive carries it.

meeting_date_local.title: Meeting Date Local
meeting_date_local.description: Meeting date in the venue's own time zone, YYYY-MM-DD. For GB and IE racing key on race_id or (venue, meeting_date_local, race_number). Absent until the archive carries it.

ClosingLineRow.title: ClosingLineRow
ClosingLineRow.description:
One archived series: a race, a runner and a bookmaker. Field order is the CSV column order.

Every field is nullable in the schema; the ones described as "never null" are always set on a
served row.

total_rows.title: Total Rows
total_rows.description: Rows matching the filter before limit/offset

archive_from.title: Archive From
archive_from.description: Earliest start_time in the whole archive. The archive only grows; this is its true floor as of right now, not a promise.

window_days.title: Window Days
window_days.description: Set when the caller's plan clamps the lookback. NULL means the full archive was searched.

resulted_rows.title: Resulted Rows
resulted_rows.description: Rows in the matching set that have a result_status. Published because result coverage is thin and growing (5.3% of archived races on 2026-08-18) — do not assume a NULL finish_position means the runner lost. It means no position was published for the runner: harness and NZ results named the placegetters only before 2026-10-04 and carry the full field from then, while AU thoroughbred and greyhound results position every finisher (from 2026-09-14).

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: Your own id for this bet, echoed back unchanged.

race_id.title: Race Id
race_id.description: The race_id from /v1/racing/next-to-go, /events, /results or the archive. The most reliable way to name a race; use venue + meeting_date + race_number only when you do not hold it.

venue.title: Venue
venue.description: Venue name as our feeds spell it (case-insensitive). Needs meeting_date and race_number.

runner_ref.title: Runner Ref
runner_ref.description: Registry id as served on /results and the archive — ra:<horsecode> or grv:<dogId>. Exact match; the most reliable way to name a runner.

runner_name.title: Runner Name
runner_name.description: Runner name; matched the same way the feeds match names (case, punctuation and country suffixes ignored).

bookmaker.title: Bookmaker
bookmaker.description: bookmaker_key the bet was struck with. When given, `clv_pct` is measured against THAT book's closing price and `close_book` is filled; when absent, against the market reference chosen by `reference`.

stake.title: Stake
stake.description: Stake for the P&L line. Defaults to one flat unit.

resolved.title: Resolved
resolved.description: True when the race AND the runner were found in the archive. False rows carry `reason` and no numbers.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: race_not_found · race_ambiguous · runner_not_found · runner_ambiguous · bookmaker_withheld · no_closing_line · no_closing_line_for_book.

close_book.title: Close Book
close_book.description: The named bookmaker's closing win price, when it recorded a closing line.

close_best.title: Close Best
close_best.description: Highest closing win price across books.

close_median.title: Close Median
close_median.description: Median closing win price across books.

books_at_close.title: Books At Close
books_at_close.description: Books with a closing line for this runner.

close_reference.title: Close Reference
close_reference.description: The close `clv_pct` is measured against: close_book when a bookmaker was named and priced the close, else the market reference.

clv_pct.title: Clv Pct
clv_pct.description: (price_taken / close_reference − 1) × 100. Positive means you beat the close.

won.title: Won
won.description: On a final result: true for the winner, false for every other runner — including one with no published position, since results list placegetters only. Null until final, and null when the result records no winner.

pnl.title: Pnl
pnl.description: stake × (price − 1) on a win, −stake on a loss, null until the result is final.

reference.title: Reference
reference.description: The market close used when a bet names no bookmaker, and reported as close_best / close_median on every bet regardless: `best` is the highest closing win price across books, `median` the median.

archive_floor.title: Archive Floor
archive_floor.description: Earliest race day the archive holds; bets before it cannot resolve.

scored.title: Scored
scored.description: Bets with a closing line to measure against.

resulted.title: Resulted
resulted.description: Scored-or-resolved bets with a final result.

overround_pct.title: Overround Pct
overround_pct.description: Σ 1/price × 100 over the runners this book priced; null below two.

included.title: Included
included.description: Whether this book entered the consensus.

best_price_market_pct.title: Best Price Market Pct
best_price_market_pct.description: Σ 1/best_price × 100 over the runners with a consensus. Under 100 means the best prices across the included books beat the field.

consensus_sum_before_normalisation.title: Consensus Sum Before Normalisation
consensus_sum_before_normalisation.description: The sum of the per-runner medians before the field was scaled to one. Close to 1.0 when the books agree on the field; printed so the scaling is visible rather than silent.

field_size.title: Field Size
field_size.description: Runners a complete-field book prices; books quoting fewer are excluded as partial_field.

excluded_quotes.title: Excluded Quotes
excluded_quotes.description: Placeholder prices left out of the consensus quote by quote, on the rule /v1/racing/best-odds uses: a long price at least four times the median of three or more other books on the same runner.

twin_race_ids.title: Twin Race Ids
twin_race_ids.description: Other race_ids under which some books list THIS race (same venue, date, number, code and field): a delayed meeting while the books disagree on its start time, or one book filing it under the wrong code. Named by venue, the race most books price is served and its twins are listed here, rather than a 409. Empty when the race has none, and always empty for a call by race_id (since 2026-10-28).

no_vig_prob.title: No Vig Prob
no_vig_prob.description: This book's probability for the runner after its own margin is removed by the stated method.

secs_to_jump.title: Secs To Jump
secs_to_jump.description: Negative once the race has jumped.

refresh_tier.title: Refresh Tier
refresh_tier.description: The race's own refresh rule — live inside three hours of the jump, card beyond it. Each book's tier is on its own entry.

number.title: Number
number.description: Saddlecloth (box for greyhounds), voted across the books.

runner_ref.title: Runner Ref
runner_ref.description: Registry id where known: ra:<code> for a thoroughbred (Racing Australia's code, new each day), grv:/grsa: for a dog.

horse_ref.title: Horse Ref
horse_ref.description: pe:<name>, the stable thoroughbred identity. Null off AU thoroughbreds.

consensus_prob.title: Consensus Prob
consensus_prob.description: The market's implied probability for this runner after margin is removed from every included book and the books are combined by median, renormalised so the field sums to one. Null when fewer than `min_books` included books quote the runner. It describes the market, not the outcome.

best_price.title: Best Price
best_price.description: Highest price among the included books.

best_vs_consensus_pct.title: Best Vs Consensus Pct
best_vs_consensus_pct.description: best_price / consensus_price - 1, in percent. Negative is normal: every quoted price carries margin, so the best quote usually sits below the market's margin-free price (about -20 % on a 130 % greyhound market). It turns positive only when one book prices a runner above the panel's margin-free view. Not a value judgement.

status.title: Status
status.description: The result's own status: interim or final. An interim dividend can still move.

race_id.title: Race Id
race_id.description: Our race_id. Null on an acceptance-only answer (`card_source: acceptances`): the race is on Racing Australia's card but no bookmaker has framed it yet, and every AU book frames a race 16 hours before its jump.

start_time.title: Start Time
start_time.description: Scheduled start, UTC. Null on an acceptance-only answer; see `start_time_local`.

start_time_local.title: Start Time Local
start_time_local.description: Racing Australia's published start on the venue's own clock ('1:35PM'). Set on an acceptance-only answer.

meeting_date.title: Meeting Date
meeting_date.description: Sydney calendar date of the meeting; the London date for a British or Irish race.

track_condition.title: Track Condition
track_condition.description: As the live card or the result carries it.

race_status.title: Race Status
race_status.description: The live race's status while it is open; the result's (`interim`/`final`) once it has been run.

card_source.title: Card Source
card_source.description: `live` -- the field came from the live card; `results` -- the race has been run, its live rows are gone, and the field is the settled result's; `acceptances` -- no bookmaker has framed the race yet (or no live field is held), and the field is Racing Australia's acceptance card.

acceptances_folded.title: Acceptances Folded
acceptances_folded.description: True when Racing Australia's acceptance card for this race was found and folded in: every accepted runner (emergencies aside) is in `runners`, named as RA names it.

form_as_at.title: Form As At
form_as_at.description: This race's start, UTC. Every run and every figure below is from BEFORE this instant, so a race already run answers with what was knowable at the jump and never with its own result. On an acceptance-only answer, Sydney midnight opening the meeting day.

runs_per_runner.title: Runs Per Runner
runs_per_runner.description: The `runs` limit this answer was built with.

runners_with_runs.title: Runners With Runs
runners_with_runs.description: Runners with at least one start held (`runs_total` of 1 or more). A runner whose only held rows are scratchings is not counted.

twin_race_ids.title: Twin Race Ids
twin_race_ids.description: Other race_ids under which some books list THIS race (same venue, date, number, code and field): a delayed meeting while the books disagree on its start time, or one book filing it under the wrong code. Named by venue, the race most books price is served and its twins are listed here, rather than a 409. Empty when the race has none, and always empty for a call by race_id (since 2026-10-28).

number.title: Number
number.description: Saddlecloth number on this race's card.

name.title: Name
name.description: The horse's name as the card (or the result) spells it.

horse_ref.title: Horse Ref
horse_ref.description: `pe:<name>` -- the identity the runs were gathered on, the same value every thoroughbred surface publishes. Pass it to /v1/racing/horses/runs or /v1/racing/horses/form for the one-horse view.

runner_ref.title: Runner Ref
runner_ref.description: The Racing Australia code this runner carries on the live card or the result -- on race day the join to /v1/racing/next-to-go, /v1/racing/acceptances and /v1/racing/results. Not a horse identity: Racing Australia issues a new code for the same horse each day. Null when the card did not carry one.

barrier.title: Barrier
barrier.description: Barrier drawn for THIS race, as the card publishes it (the stall draw on a British or Irish card).

weight_kg.title: Weight Kg
weight_kg.description: Weight allotted for THIS race, as the card publishes it; a British or Irish card's stones and pounds converted to kg, one decimal.

age.title: Age
age.description: The horse's age as the card prints it. British and Irish cards (William Hill, Betway) publish it; the Australian books do not, so it is null on an AU race.

rating.title: Rating
rating.description: The rating the card prints: on a British or Irish race the Racing Post rating as William Hill's card carries it. Null when no card we read publishes one (every AU race).

scratched.title: Scratched
scratched.description: True when the card has scratched the horse. It stays in the field so the runners match what the acceptances published.

last10.title: Last10
last10.description: Racing Australia's last-ten figures for the horse, as its acceptance card prints them; on a British or Irish race the form figures the bookmaker's card prints (William Hill, Betway). Null when no card lists this runner, or lists no figures.

last_start_date.title: Last Start Date
last_start_date.description: The horse's last start as Racing Australia's acceptance card gives it, YYYY-MM-DD, including starts older than `source.coverage_from`: a runner with `runs_total` 0 and a last start before that floor has history we do not hold (read it with /v1/racing/horses/form). Null with `last10` null: the card shows no previous start.

runs_total.title: Runs Total
runs_total.description: STARTS we hold for this horse before this race's start: runs with `status` `ran`, the same count as `stats.starts`. A scratching is not a start. 0 is honest: no start held -- a first starter, or a horse whose starts predate `source.coverage_from` (on an Australian race `last_start_date` tells the two apart). Before 2026-10-13 this counted every held row, scratchings included, so a horse scratched before its debut read 1 or more: on 2026-10-12, 442 of the 31,163 horses in the store held scratchings and no start. That count is `held_rows_total`.

held_rows_total.title: Held Rows Total
held_rows_total.description: Every row we hold for this horse before this race's start: its starts plus its scratchings (rows whose `status` is not `ran`). `runs` is drawn from these rows, so a horse with `runs_total` 0 can still carry `runs` entries -- its scratchings. Measured on 2026-10-12, 61,719 of the store's 282,639 rows (21.8%) were scratchings.

stats.description: Over every held run before this race, not just the `runs` returned; starts only.

runs.title: Runs
runs.description: Newest first, at most `runs` of them, every one before this race's start. Scratchings are included and read `status: scratched`.

meeting_date.title: Meeting Date
meeting_date.description: Sydney calendar date of the meeting; the London date for a British or Irish race.

race_status.title: Race Status
race_status.description: The live race's status while it is open; the result's (`interim`/`final`) once it has been run.

card_source.title: Card Source
card_source.description: `live` -- the field came from the live card; `results` -- the race has been run, its live rows are gone, and the field is the settled result's.

form_as_at.title: Form As At
form_as_at.description: This race's start, UTC. Every run and figure below is from BEFORE this instant, so a race already run answers with what was knowable at the jump, never its own result.

runners_with_runs.title: Runners With Runs
runners_with_runs.description: Runners with at least one start held (`runs_total` of 1 or more). A runner whose only held rows are scratchings or unused reserves is not counted.

number.title: Number
number.description: Rug number on this race's card.

name.title: Name
name.description: The dog's name as the card (or the result) spells it.

name_key.title: Name Key
name_key.description: The identity the runs were grouped on (letters and digits). Pass it, or the name, as `dog` to /v1/racing/greyhounds/form or /stats for the one-dog view.

box.title: Box
box.description: Trap drawn for THIS race: the book's draw where it gives one, else the rug number (on a British or Irish card the two are the same number).

form.title: Form
form.description: The card's form figures as the bookmaker prints them (William Hill and PointsBet on British and Irish cards; PointsBet on Australian ones). Null on a race answered from its result.

scratched.title: Scratched
scratched.description: True when the card has scratched the dog, or it is an unused reserve. It stays in the field.

runner_ref.title: Runner Ref
runner_ref.description: Registry id (grv:/grsa:) carried by a settled Australian result; null on a live card, on every British or Irish race, and on an Australian result filled from PointsBet's settled race card (Victorian tracks from the 2026-10-14 card).

runs_total.title: Runs Total
runs_total.description: STARTS we hold for this dog BEFORE this race's start: runs with `status` `ran`, the same count as `stats.starts`. A scratching or an unused reserve is not a start. 0 is honest: a first starter, or a record older than `source.coverage_from`. Before 2026-10-13 this counted every held row; that count is `held_rows_total`.

held_rows_total.title: Held Rows Total
held_rows_total.description: Every row we hold for this dog before this race's start: its starts plus its scratchings and unused reserves (rows whose `status` is not `ran`). `runs` is drawn from these rows, so a dog with `runs_total` 0 can still carry `runs` entries. Measured 2026-10-13: 6,247 of the AU store's 103,553 rows were not starts.

stats.description: Over every held run before this race; starts only.

runs.title: Runs
runs.description: Newest first, at most `runs` of them, every one before this race's start. Scratchings and unused reserves are included and say so in `status`.

feed.title: Feed
feed.description: Where the data comes from: our own collection of published AU greyhound results, every state but Victoria via the national results pages (runner_ref grsa:), Victorian tracks via FastTrack to the 2026-10-13 card (runner_ref grv:) and via PointsBet's settled race card from the 2026-10-14 card (`source: pointsbetau`: position, box and trainer, with no registry ref, times, splits or SP). Runs on or after `results_from` are races we settled ourselves; earlier runs are the same pages read back by our history collector. Refreshed hourly. On a British or Irish race (/v1/racing/greyhounds/field, from 2026-10-12) `region` reads GB-IE and the runs are our own GB/IE results from PointsBet's settled race card, read live.

coverage_from.title: Coverage From
coverage_from.description: Sydney date of the OLDEST run in the store. A dog's record here starts here.

results_from.title: Results From
results_from.description: Sydney date our own settled results begin. A run on or after it has `origin: results` and a `result_id` that joins to /v1/racing/results; an earlier one has `origin: history` and does not.

coverage_to.title: Coverage To
coverage_to.description: Sydney date of the latest race in the store.

collectors.title: Collectors
collectors.description: Which of our collectors can contribute a run: `fasttrack` = Victorian tracks to the 2026-10-13 card, `grsa` = every other state, `pointsbetau` = PointsBet's settled race card: Victorian tracks from the 2026-10-14 card and any AU race the national pages left empty.

refreshed_hourly.title: Refreshed Hourly
refreshed_hourly.description: The store is rebuilt from our results at :58 each hour, after both collectors have written.

note.title: Note
note.description: Set on a British or Irish race: GB/IE positions are placings, so a `ran` run with a null position was not placed. Null on an Australian race.

GreyhoundFieldSource.title: GreyhoundFieldSource
GreyhoundFieldSource.description:
The field view's source block: the per-dog one plus `note`. A subclass, so the per-dog routes'
published shape does not change.

places.title: Places
places.description: Finishes in the first three, wins included.

dog.title: Dog
dog.description: The dog's name as our results spell it.

name_key.title: Name Key
name_key.description: The identity the runs were grouped on (letters and digits).

runner_refs.title: Runner Refs
runner_refs.description: Every registry id seen for this name, across both collectors.

runs_total.title: Runs Total
runs_total.description: STARTS we hold for this dog since `source.coverage_from`: runs with `status` `ran`, the same count as /v1/racing/greyhounds/stats `overall.starts`. A scratching or an unused reserve is not a start. Before 2026-10-13 this counted every held row; that count is `held_rows_total`.

held_rows_total.title: Held Rows Total
held_rows_total.description: Every row we hold for this dog since `source.coverage_from`: its starts plus its scratchings and unused reserves (rows whose `status` is not `ran`). `runs` is the newest `limit` of these rows. Measured 2026-10-13: 6,247 of the store's 103,553 rows were not starts, and 102 of its 12,191 dogs held rows but no start.

date.title: Date
date.description: Sydney calendar date of the race; the London date on a British or Irish run.

number.title: Number
number.description: Rug number; equals box for a starter.

position.title: Position
position.description: Finishing place. Null when the dog did not run (see `status`) or did not complete the course. On a British or Irish run the positions are placings, so null with `status: ran` means not placed (see `source.note` on /v1/racing/greyhounds/field).

status.title: Status
status.description: `ran`, `scratched`, or `reserve` (a rug 9/10 reserve that never got a box).

margin.title: Margin
margin.description: Lengths behind the winner as the source printed it; the winner's own row carries the winning margin on Victorian tracks and null elsewhere.

time_s.title: Time S
time_s.description: The dog's own finish time in seconds.

first_split_s.title: First Split S
first_split_s.description: First sectional in seconds, as the source page printed it. Null where it printed none — a reserve that never started has none, and some tracks publish no sectionals at all.

second_split_s.title: Second Split S
second_split_s.description: Second sectional in seconds. Null on every Victorian run: FastTrack publishes one split, not two.

weight_kg.title: Weight Kg
weight_kg.description: Race-day weight in kilograms. Null where the page prints no weight — Western Australian meetings mostly print none (measured 2026-09-28 over 2026-09-13..28: Cannington 2.5%, Mandurah 15.4%, Northam 68.7% of runs).

pir.title: Pir
pir.description: Position in running as TEXT, one digit per in-running mark ("21" = 2nd then 1st at the marks; the finish is not a mark). Victorian runs: FastTrack's own PIR column. Other states, since 2026-09-29: the national page's In Race Positions card, which only some tracks print — measured 2026-09-28 over the 158 national races of 2026-09-27..28: NSW 79.6%, QLD 79.0%, WA 100% of runs, SA and TAS about 0% (no card at Angle Park, Gawler, Launceston, Rockhampton or Temora). The two sources' marks are not the same points on a track: compare PIR within one source. Null where the page printed none.

grade.title: Grade
grade.description: The race's grade in the SOURCE'S OWN WORDS — "M", "4/5", "FFA" on the national pages, a race type like "Tier 3 - Maiden" on FastTrack. The two vocabularies are NOT mapped onto each other and must not be compared across states. Null on runs whose field was stored before 2026-09-21.

win_time_s.title: Win Time S
win_time_s.description: The winner's time in the same race, so `time_s - win_time_s` is the deficit.

sp.title: Sp
sp.description: Official starting price, decimal return on $1. Null = unknown, never zero.

field_size.title: Field Size
field_size.description: Dogs that ran in that race.

runner_ref.title: Runner Ref
runner_ref.description: Registry id of the dog as the collector for that track numbers it: grv:<id> or grsa:<id>. Null on a run filled from PointsBet's settled race card (Victorian tracks from the 2026-10-14 card), which numbers no registry.

source.title: Source
source.description: Which collector wrote the race: `fasttrack` or `grsa`, or `pointsbetau` for a run from PointsBet's settled race card — every British or Irish run, and an Australian run it filled (Victorian tracks from the 2026-10-14 card), which carries no registry ref, time, split, weight, PIR, grade or SP.

origin.title: Origin
origin.description: `results` — the race is one we settled and serve on /v1/racing/results; `history` — the race was read back off the same official results page by our history collector and has no results row.

result_id.title: Result Id
result_id.description: Id of the /v1/racing/results row this run came from. On an `origin: history` run it is a synthetic `hist:…` id that joins to nothing.

grade.title: Grade
grade.description: Set when `by` includes grade: the race's grade in the source's own words ("5", "M", "4/5" nationally; a race type like "Grade 5" or "Mixed 4/5" on FastTrack). The two vocabularies are NOT mapped onto each other, so compare rows within one source. A run stored with no grade groups under null.

starts.title: Starts
starts.description: Runs with status `ran` — scratchings and unused reserves are excluded from every figure here.

places.title: Places
places.description: Finishes in the first three, wins included.

avg_time_s.title: Avg Time S
avg_time_s.description: Over the runs with a recorded time.

avg_first_split_s.title: Avg First Split S
avg_first_split_s.description: Mean first sectional over the runs in this group that carry one. Null when none does — the count behind it is not `starts`, because some tracks publish no sectionals.

avg_sp.title: Avg Sp
avg_sp.description: Mean official starting price over the runs that carry one.

last_start.title: Last Start
last_start.description: Sydney date of the most recent run in the group.

by.title: By
by.description: The dimensions the rows are grouped by, in the order given.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: One row per distinct combination, most starts first.

overall.description: The same figures over every run since `source.coverage_from`.

runner_ref.title: Runner Ref
runner_ref.description: A Racing Australia code for this horse. `candidates` is always empty: a name resolves to one horse. See `ambiguous`.

last_seen.title: Last Seen
last_seen.description: Most recent date this ref appeared on our feeds (acceptance or result).

source.title: Source
source.description: Where it was seen: acceptances or results.

splits.title: Splits
splits.description: RA's own career splits, keyed first_up, second_up, firm, good, soft, heavy, synthetic — plus track, distance and track_distance when RA renders them. Each value is starts/wins/seconds/thirds.

horse_ref.title: Horse Ref
horse_ref.description: The HORSE: `pe:<name>`, the registered name folded to letters and digits. The same value on /v1/racing/results runners and placings, the live board, the closing-line and price-path archives, /v1/racing/horses/runs and the form backfill — and accepted as `horse` here. This is the key to join a horse across meetings.

runner_ref.title: Runner Ref
runner_ref.description: The Racing Australia code the page was read under — the most recent code we hold for the horse. Racing Australia issues a new code for the same horse each day, so it is not a horse identity — `horse_ref` is.

ambiguous.title: Ambiguous
ambiguous.description: ALWAYS FALSE since 2026-09-21, and kept only so that callers reading it do not break. A name now resolves to one horse: several ra: codes under one name are the ordinary case (they are entry codes), not two horses. `candidates` is empty with it.

profile.colours: Lime, Purple And Gold Braces And Armbands

last_gear_change.title: Last Gear Change
last_gear_change.description: As published, date and gear, e.g. '20-Aug-2026, Blinkers, First Time, ...'.

venue.title: Venue
venue.description: Venue name. Set when `source.feed` is 'puntersedge_results'; RA's own page gives the compressed `track` code instead and leaves this null.

origin.title: Origin
origin.description: Set on a run that came from OUR OWN collected results rather than RA's page: every run when `source.feed` is 'puntersedge_results', and the newer runs added on top of a stored RA copy (`source.own_runs_added`). 'results' (our own settled results), 'history' (collected afterwards from RA's results page) or 'tabtouch' (the TABtouch results backfill). Null on a run read from RA's page.

track.title: Track
track.description: RA's compressed track code as published ('W FM' is Warwick Farm, 'RAND' Randwick).

meet_code.title: Meet Code
meet_code.description: RA meeting code; every runner in the same meeting shares it.

trial.title: Trial
trial.description: True for an unofficial run, a barrier trial or a jump-out: $0 prize, 0kg weights and no market are how RA publishes them. Not a race start; RA's `career` does not count them. Jump-outs read false before 2026-10-26.

trial_kind.title: Trial Kind
trial_kind.description: 'barrier_trial' or 'jump_out' when `trial` is true (RA's T and J flags in `result_raw`), else null.

result_raw.title: Result Raw
result_raw.description: The position cell as published, kept for rows that don't parse to a number.

going.title: Going
going.description: Condition word: Firm, Good, Soft, Heavy, Synthetic.

going_rating.title: Going Rating
going_rating.description: The number after the condition (Soft7 -> 7). Null where RA prints none.

race_class.title: Race Class
race_class.description: RA's official class string for that race: 'MDN-SW', 'CTRY MDN', 'BM64', '3Y MDN-TRL'.

prize_won.title: Prize Won
prize_won.description: This horse's cut, when RA shows it.

jockey_code.title: Jockey Code
jockey_code.description: RA's stable jockey code, consistent across every page that names the same rider.

trainer.title: Trainer
trainer.description: Trainer of the day for THIS run, filled from our own results archive — RA's form table never names the trainer per run. Populated for runs from 2026-09-01 onward (the archive's full-runner floor) and NULL before that; `profile.trainer` is the horse's current trainer, which is usually but not always the same person.

sectional_distance_m.title: Sectional Distance M
sectional_distance_m.description: The published closing sectional's distance, usually 600.

margin_l.title: Margin L
margin_l.description: Margin in lengths. On this horse's own win it is the winning margin over the runner-up.

pir.title: Pir
pir.description: Position in running at the published marks (800m/400m).

prices.title: Prices
prices.description: The published price path, opening quote through SP, oldest first.

sp.title: Sp
sp.description: Starting price — the last entry of `prices`.

placegetters.title: Placegetters
placegetters.description: The two nearest finishers RA lists (2nd and 3rd on this horse's win; the winner and runner-up otherwise), each with its own ra: code.

date.title: Date
date.description: Sydney calendar date of the race; the London date for a British or Irish race (/v1/racing/form, 2026-10-12).

track_condition.title: Track Condition
track_condition.description: As published for the meeting, e.g. 'Good 4'.

box.title: Box
box.description: Barrier. Null on a scratching — a runner that never jumped has no barrier.

position.title: Position
position.description: Finishing place. Null when the horse did not start (see `status`) or started and did not finish (see `abnormal`).

abnormal.title: Abnormal
abnormal.description: Racing Australia's own Finish cell whenever it is not a number, passed through verbatim (Fell, PulledUp, TailedOff, LR, FF, LP, and 'SB' for scratched at the barrier). THERE IS NO CLOSED LIST — an unseen code reaches you unchanged. Read it with `status`.

margin.title: Margin
margin.description: Lengths behind the winner as RA printed it ('0.75L'); null where it prints none.

time_s.title: Time S
time_s.description: The horse's own time in seconds, which RA publishes for the WINNER only: since 29 September 2026 a position-1 run carries the race time from RA's race header (the same value as `race_time_s`); every other run's is null, because RA's results table prints no per-runner time and a beaten horse's time is not the race time. Null on runs stored before then until that meeting is re-read.

sp.title: Sp
sp.description: Official starting price, decimal return on $1. Null = unknown, never zero.

sp_note.title: Sp Note
sp_note.description: RA's favouritism marker: 'F' favourite, 'EF' equal favourite; null otherwise.

trainer.title: Trainer
trainer.description: Trainer of the day for THIS run, as the result published it.

jockey.title: Jockey
jockey.description: Rider of the day for THIS run.

field_size.title: Field Size
field_size.description: Horses that ran in that race.

weight_kg.title: Weight Kg
weight_kg.description: Allotted weight in kg, as RA's results page prints it. Kept since 28 September 2026. On origin tabtouch runs, and on runs from 10 August to 27 September 2026 whose result lacked one, it is the weight TABtouch's race page printed for the starter. Null on a scratching and where neither source had one.

carried_kg.title: Carried Kg
carried_kg.description: Weight the horse actually carried, printed by RA only when it differs from the allotted weight ('58kg (cd 56kg)'): usually an apprentice's claim (under), sometimes a rider's overweight (over), so do not assume the sign. Null when RA printed none; read coalesce(carried_kg, weight_kg) for what was carried.

race_class.title: Race Class
race_class.description: The race's class as RA's own leading conditions term -- 'Maiden', 'BenchMark 64', 'Class 1', 'Group 1' -- mechanical, never inferred, on runs stored since 28 September 2026 and on origin history runs. On origin tabtouch runs, and on runs from 10 August to 27 September 2026, it is TABtouch's class line as printed -- 'BM58 HCP', 'MDN-SW', 'GROUP 1 3UP HCP' -- so normalise the two wordings before comparing classes across runs. Null where neither source had one.

race_time_s.title: Race Time S
race_time_s.description: The race's winning time in seconds, from RA's race header ('Time: 0:58.69' -> 58.69). The same on every run of that race. Kept since 29 September 2026: null on a run stored before then until that meeting is re-read.

last_600m_s.title: Last 600M S
last_600m_s.description: The race's last-600m time in seconds, from the same header ('Last 600m: 0:34.49' -> 34.49) -- the leader's closing sectional as RA times it, a RACE figure, not this horse's own. Kept since 29 September 2026.

prize_total.title: Prize Total
prize_total.description: Total prize money of the race in AUD, from RA's prize line ('Of $30,000.'). Kept since 29 September 2026.

prize_won.title: Prize Won
prize_won.description: Place money this horse won in AUD, read off the same prize line by its finishing place ('1st $15,000, 2nd $5,300, ...'); dead-heaters share the places they tie for equally. 0 for a finish outside the places RA lists as paid; null for a horse with no finishing place (scratched, fell) or a race whose prize line was not read. Excludes bonuses and welfare-fund amounts. Kept since 29 September 2026.

runner_ref.title: Runner Ref
runner_ref.description: The Racing Australia code our results collector published for this run, from race day — the same value on the matching /v1/racing/results runner and in the archives for that race. Racing Australia issues a new code for the same horse each day, so it differs from run to run: group a horse's runs on `horse_ref`, not on this.

horse_ref.title: Horse Ref
horse_ref.description: The horse this run belongs to: `pe:<name>`, the registered name folded to letters and digits. Identical on every run of the same horse, and the same value /v1/racing/results runners and placings, the live board, the closing-line and price-path archives and /v1/racing/horses/form carry — the key that joins a horse across meetings, where `runner_ref` joins the rows about one race.

result_id.title: Result Id
result_id.description: Id of the /v1/racing/results row this run came from. A run with origin 'history' or 'tabtouch' carries a synthetic 'hist:...' id that joins to /v1/racing/results on nothing.

origin.title: Origin
origin.description: 'results' -- from our own settled results (/v1/racing/results). 'history' -- collected afterwards from Racing Australia's results page for a race held before our live results began: same fields, no /v1/racing/results row behind it. 'tabtouch' -- collected afterwards from TABtouch's public race page for a race older than Racing Australia's results pages reach (about fifteen months back): number, rider, barrier, weight, trainer and the first four placings, so position null there means unplaced; no margin, time or sp.

horse.title: Horse
horse.description: The horse's name as our results spell it.

name_key.title: Name Key
name_key.description: The identity the runs were grouped on (letters and digits).

horse_ref.title: Horse Ref
horse_ref.description: `name_key` as the identifier every thoroughbred surface publishes: `pe:<name_key>`. Pass it back here, or to /v1/racing/horses/form, and read it off /v1/racing/results runners and placings, the live board and the closing-line and price-path archives to gather one horse across meetings.

runner_refs.title: Runner Refs
runner_refs.description: Every Racing Australia horsecode our results published under this name, sorted. Several is normal, not an error — see `runs[].runner_ref`.

runs_total.title: Runs Total
runs_total.description: STARTS held for this horse since `source.coverage_from`: runs with `status` `ran`, the same count as `stats.starts`. A scratching is not a start. Before 2026-10-13 this counted every held row, scratchings included; that count is `held_rows_total`.

held_rows_total.title: Held Rows Total
held_rows_total.description: Every row held for this horse since `source.coverage_from`, scratchings included. `runs` is the newest `limit` of THESE rows, so page on this, not on `runs_total`. Measured on 2026-10-12, 61,719 of the store's 282,639 rows (21.8%) were scratchings.

stats.description: Over EVERY held run, not just the ones returned.

starts.title: Starts
starts.description: Runs with status `ran` — scratchings are excluded from every figure here. Equal to `runs_total` since 2026-10-13; `held_rows_total` counts the scratchings too, which is why it can be higher.

places.title: Places
places.description: Finishes in the first three, wins included.

feed.title: Feed
feed.description: 'racing_australia' -- Racing Australia's own form page (profile, career, full run lines). 'puntersedge_results' -- RA was not serving this horse's page and no stored copy existed, so `runs` is the horse's record in OUR OWN collected results instead; `profile` and `career` are then null, and `note` says what the runs cover.

note.title: Note
note.description: Set with feed 'puntersedge_results': what these runs are, and what they are not. Also set when `own_runs_added` is above 0.

fetched_at.title: Fetched At
fetched_at.description: UTC time this horse's page was last read from RA. With feed 'puntersedge_results' (since 2026-10-26; null before): the UTC time these runs were read from our own results store, which is rebuilt hourly — `coverage_to` says how far it reaches.

stale.title: Stale
stale.description: True when RA could not be reached just now and this is the stored copy served past its six-hour refresh window. Runs the horse has had since that copy was read are added from our own results — see `own_runs_added`.

own_runs_added.title: Own Runs Added
own_runs_added.description: Runs from OUR OWN collected results added at the top of `runs` because they are newer than the stored RA page (each carries `venue` and `origin`; RA fields we do not collect are null). `career` and `profile` are still as of `fetched_at` and do not include them. 0 when the page is current.

coverage_to.title: Coverage To
coverage_to.description: Feed 'puntersedge_results' only: Sydney date of the latest race in our own results store.

window.title: Window
window.description: Whether the 60-minute capture window is open for this race, when its first tick landed, and which marks could be evaluated.

market.title: Market
market.description: Race level: best-price market percentage now and at T-15 / T-60, the favourite now and at T-10, and the books behind the consensus.

runners.title: Runners
runners.description: One object per runner, favourite first: consensus at each mark with high and low, time-anchored moves, breadth, first mover and the signal class.

twin_race_ids.title: Twin Race Ids
twin_race_ids.description: Other race_ids under which some books list THIS race (same venue, date, number, code and field): a delayed meeting while the books disagree on its start time, or one book filing it under the wrong code. Named by venue, the race most books price is served and its twins are listed here, rather than a 409. Empty when the race has none, and always empty for a call by race_id (since 2026-10-28).

overround_pct.title: Overround Pct
overround_pct.description: Sum of 1/price across this book's quoted runners, as a percentage. Null when fewer than two runners are quoted, where the figure would describe nothing.

observed_at.title: Observed At
