observed_at.description: Newest price change this book made on this race, UTC.

places.title: Places
places.description: Runners the bet covers: 1 for win, the race's places_paid for place, 2/3/4 for the Same Race Multi legs. Null when the race never reported places_paid.

suspect.title: Suspect
suspect.description: Quotes kept out of `best` (since 2026-10-20) by the same rules as /v1/racing/best-odds `suspect_win`: each entry is number, name, bookmaker, price, and either `consensus` alone (a placeholder price, 4x or more the median of the other books) or a `reason` (pre_scratching, book_under_round, book_not_repriced) with the figure behind it. The quote itself is still listed under `bookmakers`.

runner_ref.title: Runner Ref
runner_ref.description: Registry id — ra:<horsecode> or grv:<dogId> — where one is known.

horse_ref.title: Horse Ref
horse_ref.description: pe:<name>, the stable thoroughbred identity. Null off AU thoroughbreds.

source_url.title: Source Url
source_url.description: The book's own page for this race. Present while the market is open (source is live); null on a race answered from the stored close, which keeps the prices and the runner identities but not the links.

source_link.title: Source Link
source_link.description: Your own link for this price: source_url built through the link templates stored with PUT /v1/link-templates (since 2026-10-14). Absent when your account stores none, or there is nothing to link.

total_rows.title: Total Rows
total_rows.description: Rows matching the filter before limit/offset.

summary_from.title: Summary From
summary_from.description: Earliest start_time in the table. The summary is built from the 45-day tick store, so it begins where that store stood when the job first ran.

window_days.title: Window Days
window_days.description: Set when the caller's plan clamps the lookback. NULL means the whole table.

twin_race_ids.title: Twin Race Ids
twin_race_ids.description: Other race_ids under which some books list THIS race (same venue, date, number, code and field): a delayed meeting while the books disagree on its start time, or one book filing it under the wrong code. Named by venue, the race most books price is served and its twins are listed here, rather than a 409. Empty when the race has none, and always empty for a call by race_id (since 2026-10-28).

quote_detail.title: Quote Detail
quote_detail.description: Per book and runner, the fields the book publishes beside its prices (since 2026-09-29): open_price (the book's own opening price), flucs (its fluctuations, most recent first), tote_win / tote_place (its tote dividends by product code; PROV is an indicative pre-race dividend), boost_price / boost_type, and the exchange fields. Each entry carries bookmaker, number, name, runner_ref, seen_at (UTC, when the fields were read) and only the fields that book carries.

scratchings.title: Scratchings
scratchings.description: The race's scratched runners: name, number, barrier, scratched_at (the scratching book's own time, UTC), vacant for an empty box. Read from the open race while it is live and from the capture taken at the jump once it has been purged (from 2026-09-29).

tote_series.title: Tote Series
tote_series.description: Per book and runner, the book's tote approximates at fixed marks before the jump (since 2026-10-06): points at 3600, 1800, 900, 600, 300, 180, 120 and 60 seconds, each the first read the capture saw at or inside its mark: mark_seconds, read_at (UTC), secs_to_jump, and tote_win / tote_place by product code (PROV is an indicative pre-race dividend). The last read before the jump is tote_win / tote_place in quote_detail.

book_scratchings.title: Book Scratchings
book_scratchings.description: Per book and scratched runner (since 2026-10-06): reported_at, the first time that book's own feed listed the scratching; book_scratched_at, the scratch time the book itself states, where it carries one; first_quoted_at / last_quoted_at, when that book's feed still carried a win price for the runner after the race's scratchings named it, to the minute, with last_quoted_win (for a book that flags the scratching itself, recorded once at the flag: its price at the scratching). All UTC. Never served as a price.

books_quoting.title: Books Quoting
books_quoting.description: Books with a price for this runner, including ones we have never observed move.

books_with_history.title: Books With History
books_with_history.description: Books with two or more captured prices — the only ones that can evidence a move. The consensus and the `min_books` gate use THIS count, not `books_quoting`.

books_unchanged.title: Books Unchanged
books_unchanged.description: Books whose captured price has not moved, including books seen only once. books_firming + books_drifting + books_unchanged == books_quoting.

venue_id.title: Venue Id
venue_id.description: Stable slug for this venue spelling ('sandown-hillside'). Spelling variants of one venue share one id.

venue_canonical.title: Venue Canonical
venue_canonical.description: Canonical display name for venue_id ('Sandown Hillside').

venue_site.title: Venue Site
venue_site.description: Physical-complex key: tracks sharing one venue complex share one site ('sandown' covers Sandown, Sandown Hillside, Sandown Lakeside and the Sandown Park greyhound track).

places_paid.title: Places Paid
places_paid.description: Places the race pays, as the bookmaker supplying it states. For British and Irish races this is the each-way terms' place count (2 or 3, 4 on a 16-plus handicap) and the UK books' place_price is derived from the same terms; for Australian races it is the quoted place market's count. Null when no bookmaker on the race supplies it.

track_condition_changed_at.title: Track Condition Changed At
track_condition_changed_at.description: UTC instant of the most recent logged track-condition, weather or rail transition for this race's meeting — Racing Australia's re-published rating or a bookmaker's race page moving between two of our polls. Null when nothing has changed since we began watching the meeting. /v1/racing/track-conditions serves the sequence.

race_class.title: Race Class
race_class.description: The first term of RA's official conditions line for this race ('BenchMark 64', 'Maiden', 'Group 1') on AU thoroughbreds. US and Canadian races (from 2026-10-27, and the archive cards from 2026-08-01) carry TVG's race class: 'Maiden Claiming', 'Allowance', 'Stakes', or on harness cards the gait, 'Pace' or 'Trot'. Null elsewhere.

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.description: RA's official conditions line, verbatim — class, race type, minimum weight, age/sex restrictions, claiming allowances. On a US or Canadian race, TVG's race description verbatim (from 2026-10-27, archive cards from 2026-08-01); on some harness cards it also carries the track's selections.

prize_total.title: Prize Total
prize_total.description: Total advertised prize for the race, whole units of `prize_currency` (AUD from Racing Australia). On a US or Canadian race, the track's advertised purse from TVG (USD in the US, CAD in Canada; from 2026-10-27, archive cards from 2026-08-01).

prize_currency.title: Prize Currency
prize_currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of `prize_total` ('AUD'); 'USD' or 'CAD' on a US or Canadian race. Null exactly when `prize_total` is null. Added 2026-10-26.

rail.title: Rail
rail.description: Rail position for the meeting, as RA publishes it ('+3m Entire'). AU thoroughbred only.

track_name.title: Track Name
track_name.description: Racing Australia's own name for the course this race runs on, verbatim: 'Hillside' at Sandown, 'Randwick' vs the Kensington inner course, 'Main' elsewhere. Combine with venue_site to tell dual-course meetings apart. AU thoroughbred only; null elsewhere.

market_closed_at.title: Market Closed At
market_closed_at.description: UTC time at which the market was FIRST seen shut — the book stopped taking bets on this race. Poll-observed: this is the first poll that saw the state, not the exact instant, so it lands up to one polling pass after it, and passes are most frequent in the minutes before the jump. Set once: a market that flickers SUSPENDED -> OPEN -> SUSPENDED keeps the FIRST suspension. TWO SOURCES report market state. PointsBet closes its book at the real jump — measured 2026-09-03 over 9 live races followed across their jump, 0.2 to 1.4 minutes AFTER the advertised start on AU/NZ cards — and the Betfair Exchange reports it while it quotes the market, which is until about two minutes before the jump. `market_state_source` names the one that produced this value. Exchange-sourced stamps are withheld from customer plans, so a race seen shut only by the exchange reads null. Bookmaker-sourced stamps are served to everybody. Null also means no feed observed a transition — it never means the market stayed open.

inplay_at.title: Inplay At
inplay_at.description: UTC time at which the race was FIRST seen in-play — the actual off, as opposed to `start_time`, which is the ADVERTISED off and moves. Same poll-observed, set-once semantics as `market_closed_at`, and withheld on the same source rule. Reported by the Betfair Exchange only: bookmakers do not run racing in-play, so a bookmaker feed says when it CLOSED its book, not when the race went. For a race the exchange has stopped quoting, `market_closed_at` from a bookmaker is the closest measured instant to the off.

market_state_source.title: Market State Source
market_state_source.description: Which feed's market state produced `market_closed_at` / `inplay_at` on this race — 'pointsbetau' for the bookmaker, 'betfair_ex_au' for the exchange. Set once, alongside the first stamp. Null when no transition has been observed, and null for customer plans whenever the stamps themselves are withheld, so a non-null value here is always the provenance of values you can see.

tote.title: Tote
tote.description: North American tote odds for this race, from TVG's public race board (US and Canadian thoroughbred, quarter horse and harness), or null. A tote is a pool, not a bookmaker, so it sits here and never in a runner's `bookmakers`, best_win or any bookmaker count. `runners[]` carries per betting interest `morning_line` (the track's line, set before betting) and `win_odds` (the host tote's current odds-to-1), each as TVG sends it ('5/2') and as a decimal price (`morning_line_decimal`, `win_decimal` = 1 + odds, so 5/2 is 3.5), plus `win_pool`, that runner's WIN pool money in USD. `win_odds` is null until the WIN pool opens (`pools_open`) and on a scratched runner. Pre-race the odds are an estimate of the win payoff: a tote pays what the pool pays when it closes. `status` is open, off or official; `final` marks the odds the race settled on (read once it is official). `read_at` is our read of TVG. Null on a race no TVG race links to, which is every race outside the US and Canada. Added 2026-10-27. RACE DETAILS (added the same day): `surface` (Dirt, Turf, Synthetic; after a course change, with `surface_changed_from` naming the one it left, so a race taken off the turf reads Dirt from Turf), `track_condition` (Fast, Firm, Sloppy, Good...; null where the track reports none, which is most harness cards) and `condition_changed_at` when it changed today; `pools`, every pool the track runs on the race with its money in USD ({code, name, amount}: WN win, EX exacta, TR trifecta, SU superfecta, DB daily double, P3/P4/P5 pick-N...); and on a scratched runner `scratch_reason` ('Veterinarian', 'Stewards', 'Trainer') and `scratched_at` from the track's change log. Probables and will-pays are on /v1/racing/tote?exotics=true. RUNNER CARD (added the same day): each runner also carries `jockey` (the driver on harness), `trainer`, `weight_lb`, `age`, `sex`, `sire`, `dam`, `dam_sire` and `medication` ('L' = Lasix), names as TVG prints them (surname first), null until the card is read (within minutes of the race reaching TVG's board); a coupled entry joins its horses' names with ' / ', leaves weight and age null and lists each horse in `horses`. RACE CARD (added the same day): `race_class` ('Maiden Claiming', 'Allowance', 'Stakes'; on harness the gait, 'Pace' or 'Trot'), `conditions` (TVG's race description verbatim, which on some harness cards also carries the track's selections), `purse` in `purse_currency` (the track's own: USD in the US, CAD in Canada), `claiming_price` (null on a race that is not a claimer) and `age_restriction` (TVG's code, '3U' = three-year-olds and up); null until the race's card is read.

data_age_seconds.title: Data Age Seconds
data_age_seconds.description: Age in seconds of the OLDEST bookmaker quote in this race — the staleness you are exposed to if you act on any price here. Since 2026-08-15 this is the worst leg, not the freshest; `freshest_age_seconds` carries the best-case figure.

freshest_age_seconds.title: Freshest Age Seconds
freshest_age_seconds.description: Age in seconds of the freshest bookmaker quote in this race.

refresh_tier.title: Refresh Tier
refresh_tier.description: Which refresh rule this race is on, and therefore what the race-level `stale` means. `live` = inside 3 hours of the jump: books re-price it on every 8-20s poll, and `stale` fires past 120 seconds. `card` = further out: books re-price it about every 15 minutes so a full day fits inside their rate limits, and `stale` fires past 1800 seconds. Every published quote carries ITS OWN `refresh_tier`, and it can be `card` on a `live` race: Betr's upstream rate-limits us, so that book stops re-pricing every poll 30 minutes before the jump rather than 3 hours (PlayUp, on a 6-requests-a-minute budget, at 6 minutes), and its quotes between there and 3 hours are refreshed every 5-15 minutes, published as `card`, and judged against 1800 seconds (since 2026-09-07; before that they were marked stale). A book's tier is never tighter than its race's. `age_seconds` is the TRUE age in every case — only the threshold changes.

stale.title: Stale
stale.description: True when the oldest contributing bookmaker is older than this race's `refresh_tier` threshold — 120s on `live`, 1800s on `card`. It does NOT mean the whole race is dead — read `stale_bookmakers` and each bookmaker's own `stale`/`age_seconds`.

stale_bookmakers.title: Stale Bookmakers
stale_bookmakers.description: Bookmaker keys in this race whose quote is older than the `refresh_tier` threshold (120s live, 1800s card).

checklist.detail: Your key is shown once. Revealing it again here issues a new key (the old one keeps working for 24 hours).
checklist.label: API key available

checklist.detail: Successful data requests on 7 separate days within 7 days of your first.
checklist.label: Repeat usage

routes.research: Build a personal model or research tool

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: true lets this account run past its monthly allowance, up to the ceiling, and be invoiced for the excess. false restores the hard 402 at the allowance.

state.title: State
state.description: Echo of the filter; null when a name search crossed all states.

state.title: State
state.description: AUS is the national table — RA's own combined leaderboard, not a sum of the state rows.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: RA's split: all, metro, provincial, country or picnic.

ra_code.title: Ra Code
ra_code.description: RA's stable code from the row's engagement link — the same namespace as trainer_code on acceptance data and jockey_code on /v1/racing/horses/form runs, so rows join on identity, not name spelling.

firsts.title: Firsts
firsts.description: Wins. REAL, not int: dead heats appear as halves in some tables (RA prints 23½).

period_from.title: Period From
period_from.description: Start of the window this row measures (RA seasons run 1 Aug to 31 Jul).

period_to.title: Period To
period_to.description: End of the measured window. On the running season this is the day RA rendered the table, which makes it the per-row freshness stamp: rows from a table scraped two nights ago carry that day, not today.

scraped_at.title: Scraped At
scraped_at.description: UTC time of the newest row served in this response. For the usual single-table lookup (a `state` + `scope`) every row comes from one scrape, so this IS that table's age. A `name` search spans tables scraped on different nights, so there read it as the freshest of them and use `period_to` for the age of each individual row.

top_n.title: Top N
top_n.description: RA publishes each premiership as a top-20 table. Absence from `rows` means outside the top 20, never inactivity.

history_from.title: History From
history_from.description: Start time of the earliest race this endpoint can answer for. Since 2026-09-01 races older than the ~45-day live window are served from the permanent archive, so this floor is fixed at capture start (2026-08-04) and history only deepens.

total_points.title: Total Points
total_points.description: Points matching the filter before limit/offset

race_class.title: Race Class
race_class.description: The first term of RA's official conditions line ('BenchMark 64', 'Maiden', 'Group 1') on AU thoroughbreds. US and Canadian races (from 2026-10-27, and the archive cards from 2026-08-01) carry TVG's race class: 'Maiden Claiming', 'Allowance', 'Stakes', or on harness cards the gait, 'Pace' or 'Trot'.

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.description: RA's official conditions line, verbatim. On a US or Canadian race, TVG's race description verbatim (from 2026-10-27, archive cards from 2026-08-01); on some harness cards it also carries the track's selections.

prize_total.title: Prize Total
prize_total.description: Total advertised prize, whole units of `prize_currency` (AUD from Racing Australia). On a US or Canadian race, the track's advertised purse from TVG (USD in the US, CAD in Canada; from 2026-10-27, archive cards from 2026-08-01).

prize_currency.title: Prize Currency
prize_currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of `prize_total` ('AUD'); 'USD' or 'CAD' on a US or Canadian race. Null exactly when `prize_total` is null. Added 2026-10-26.

rail.title: Rail
rail.description: Rail position for the meeting, as RA publishes it.

track_name.title: Track Name
track_name.description: RA's own name for the course this race runs on ('Hillside', 'Randwick', 'Main'). AU thoroughbred only; null elsewhere.

track_condition_changed_at.title: Track Condition Changed At
track_condition_changed_at.description: UTC instant of the most recent logged track-condition, weather or rail transition for this race's meeting; null when nothing has changed since we began watching it. The sequence is on /v1/racing/track-conditions.

status.title: Status
status.description: Set when the race row is created and revised exactly once, if at all: to 'abandoned' when Racing Australia posts an official abandoned, postponed or transferred notice for the meeting (2026-09-06). Otherwise it reads 'open' for every race in this window. It is not a live market-state signal - /v1/racing/results carries the settled status (interim, final, abandoned).

scratchings.title: Scratchings
scratchings.description: Scratched runners for this race: {name, number, barrier, scratched_at, late, emergency}. `scratched_at` (UTC) is the book's own stamp where it sends one (Ladbrokes, Neds, BetRight) and Racing Australia's official scratching sheet otherwise (AU thoroughbreds, read two-hourly); absent when neither knows. `late` marks a late scratching, `emergency` an emergency that did not gain a start. Merged across every book that reports one. Greyhound cards also carry box-vacancy placeholders here (a literal '....' or 'Vacant Box'), which are the reporting book naming an empty box rather than a withdrawn runner; match on `number` and treat a name from that set as a vacant box.

market_status.title: Market Status
market_status.description: Betting-market state (OPEN, SUSPENDED, CLOSED). Reported by PointsBet, which sends CLOSED when it shuts its book at the jump, and by the Betfair Exchange, which is withheld from customer responses pending a data licence — so a value last written by the exchange reads null. Most races are quoted by both: the exchange holds the state until about two minutes before the jump, PointsBet reports the close.

inplay.title: Inplay
inplay.description: True once the market is in-play. Exchange-only — bookmakers do not run racing in-play — so it carries the same licence hold as `market_status` and reads null for customers.

market_closed_at.title: Market Closed At
market_closed_at.description: UTC time at which the market was FIRST seen shut — the book stopped taking bets on this race. Poll-observed: this is the first poll that saw the state, not the exact instant, so it lands up to one polling pass after it, and passes are most frequent in the minutes before the jump. Set once: a market that flickers SUSPENDED -> OPEN -> SUSPENDED keeps the FIRST suspension. TWO SOURCES report market state. PointsBet closes its book at the real jump — measured 2026-09-03 over 9 live races followed across their jump, 0.2 to 1.4 minutes AFTER the advertised start on AU/NZ cards — and the Betfair Exchange reports it while it quotes the market, which is until about two minutes before the jump. `market_state_source` names the one that produced this value. Exchange-sourced stamps are withheld from customer plans, so a race seen shut only by the exchange reads null. Bookmaker-sourced stamps are served to everybody. Null also means no feed observed a transition — it never means the market stayed open.

inplay_at.title: Inplay At
inplay_at.description: UTC time at which the race was FIRST seen in-play — the actual off, as opposed to `start_time`, which is the ADVERTISED off and moves. Same poll-observed, set-once semantics as `market_closed_at`, and withheld on the same source rule. Reported by the Betfair Exchange only: bookmakers do not run racing in-play, so a bookmaker feed says when it CLOSED its book, not when the race went. For a race the exchange has stopped quoting, `market_closed_at` from a bookmaker is the closest measured instant to the off.

market_state_source.title: Market State Source
market_state_source.description: Which feed's market state produced `market_closed_at` / `inplay_at` on this race — 'pointsbetau' for the bookmaker, 'betfair_ex_au' for the exchange. Set once, alongside the first stamp. Null when no transition has been observed, and null for customer plans whenever the stamps themselves are withheld, so a non-null value here is always the provenance of values you can see.

tote_race_id.title: Tote Race Id
tote_race_id.description: TVG's race key (tvg_<track>_<date>_<n>) on a US or Canadian race, the same key /v1/racing/tote and /v1/racing/results use; it stays the same when a bookmaker starts pricing a tote-only race and `race_id` changes to the priced race's. Null outside North America and on a priced race TVG has not linked. Added 2026-10-27.

tote_only.title: Tote Only
tote_only.description: True on a North American race no bookmaker prices: it comes from TVG's race board, its `race_id` is TVG's race key (tvg_<track>_<date>_<n>, the key /v1/racing/tote and /v1/racing/results use), and price-history and next-to-go have nothing for it. Listed only when `country` names US or CA, and only for the current US race day (TVG's board). False on every other race. Added 2026-10-27.

surface.title: Surface
surface.description: Dirt, Turf or Synthetic: the surface a US or Canadian race is run on, after any course change the track logged (a turf race taken off the turf reads Dirt), from TVG. Null outside North America and on a race TVG has not linked. Added 2026-10-27.

source.title: Source
source.description: live (read from the open market) or closes (read from the stored last observation before the jump).

race_id.title: Race Id
race_id.description: Race id, joinable to /v1/racing/price-history and (while the race is still open) /v1/racing/next-to-go. Null if the race cannot be resolved in the price-history store.

coverage_from.title: Coverage From
coverage_from.description: Start time of the earliest result currently retained.

surface.title: Surface
surface.description: Dirt, Turf or Synthetic: the surface a US or Canadian race is run on, after any course change the track logged (a turf race taken off the turf reads Dirt), from TVG. Null outside North America and on a race TVG has not linked. Added 2026-10-27.

going.title: Going
going.description: Track condition word, normalised: Good, Soft, Heavy, Firm, Fast, Synthetic. Parsed from `track_condition` with the same helper /v1/racing/horses/form uses, so the two surfaces agree. Null when `track_condition` is null or unparseable; `track_condition` remains the raw string exactly as the source published it.

going_rating.title: Going Rating
going_rating.description: Numeric going rating 1-12 (the 4 in 'Good (4)'), or null. NULL IS THE MAJORITY CASE, not an exception for two rare words: most stored conditions are a bare word carrying no number at all. Measured 2026-09-10 across all 5,579 stored results, a bare 'Good' is 3,954 rows (71%) and yields null, so a rating is present on roughly 29% of rows — greyhound and other non-thoroughbred meetings publish an unrated word as a rule. A rating is never guessed from the word ('Synthetic', 67 rows, and 'Firm', 0 rows, never carry one). Separately, 205 rows store the four-character STRING 'None' in `track_condition`: `going` and `going_rating` are both null on those, while `track_condition` still serves that literal string, because `track_condition` is the raw source value passed through untouched.

places_paid.title: Places Paid
places_paid.description: Places the race paid, from the bookmakers' own terms at the close: for British and Irish races the each-way place count (2 or 3, 4 on a 16-plus handicap) of the UK-licensed books, for Australian and New Zealand races the Australian books' place market, for South African races the South African books'. It is the count most of those books paid; a tie takes the lower count, the standard terms. A book running an extra-place offer is visible in `places_paid_by_book`. It is the bookmakers' terms, not an official placings figure. Null when no book on the race gave terms, or the result is not linked to a race_id.

places_paid_by_book.title: Places Paid By Book
places_paid_by_book.description: {bookmaker_key: places} for every book on the race that gave terms at the close, including books outside the race's own region (an Australian book quoting a British race pays its own terms). Null exactly when `places_paid` is null.

race_class.title: Race Class
race_class.description: The first term of Racing Australia's official conditions line ('BenchMark 64', 'Maiden', 'Group 1'), the same value the race card carried. AU thoroughbred only, from the 2026-09-26 card; null elsewhere. No source we hold publishes race class for British or Irish races. US and Canadian races (from 2026-10-27, and the archive cards from 2026-08-01) carry TVG's race class: 'Maiden Claiming', 'Allowance', 'Stakes', or on harness cards the gait, 'Pace' or 'Trot'.

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.description: Racing Australia's official conditions line, verbatim, on AU thoroughbreds from the 2026-09-26 card. On a US or Canadian race, TVG's race description verbatim (from 2026-10-27, archive cards from 2026-08-01); on some harness cards it also carries the track's selections. Null elsewhere.

prize_total.title: Prize Total
prize_total.description: Total advertised prize for the race, whole units of `prize_currency`. AU thoroughbreds (Racing Australia) from the 2026-09-26 card. On a US or Canadian race, the track's advertised purse from TVG (USD in the US, CAD in Canada; from 2026-10-27, archive cards from 2026-08-01). Null elsewhere.

prize_currency.title: Prize Currency
prize_currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of `prize_total` ('AUD'); 'USD' or 'CAD' on a US or Canadian race. Null exactly when `prize_total` is null.

status.title: Status
status.description: interim | final | abandoned. `interim` until the placings have been stable for 30 minutes, then `final`. `abandoned` (2026-09-06) is a race that did NOT run: Racing Australia's official Abandoned & Transferred Meetings notice for that venue and date, applied to every race of the meeting — placings are empty and runners null. Settle only against `final`; treat `abandoned` as a void for settlement purposes.

status_note.title: Status Note
status_note.description: Only on `abandoned` rows: RA's own word for the non-run — "abandoned", "postponed", or "transferred to <venue>". A postponed or transferred meeting did not run at THIS venue on THIS date; if it ran elsewhere or later it appears as its own result.

placings.title: Placings
placings.description: The placegetters: {position, number, name, win_price, place_price, sp, sp_note, horse_ref}. `win_price` and `place_price` are the SETTLING BOOKMAKER'S FIXED prices. `horse_ref` (added 2026-09-21) is the same `pe:<name>` horse identity the `runners` entries carry, derived at serve time from the name on the placing and present on every placing — null off thoroughbred. It is the key that joins this placing to the same horse on another meeting; `runner_ref` on the matching `runners` entry joins the rows about this race and will not, because Racing Australia issues a new code for the same horse each day. `sp` is the OFFICIAL STARTING PRICE as a decimal return on a $1 stake (4.6 means $4.60), null where it is unknown — never 0. It is the settling market's own price, not our consensus and not a bookmaker's fixed price: thoroughbred SP comes from the Racing Australia results table, greyhound SP from our own collection of published results (Victorian tracks via FastTrack, every other state via the national results pages, both from 2026-09-13), and HARNESS SP IS ALWAYS NULL — no source we hold publishes it. `sp_note` carries Racing Australia's favouritism marker on thoroughbred runners ('F' favourite, 'EF' equal favourite) and is null everywhere else. Coverage RE-MEASURED 2026-09-08 over the whole retained store, counting only rows whose `status` is `ran` (a barrier scratching is not a starter and its price is not in this denominator): 88.6% of thoroughbred starters carry `sp` (2,105 of 2,375); on the greyhound races collected since 2026-09-13, 2,054 of 2,077 Victorian starters do (98.9%) and 4233 of 4596 of the other states' starters do (92.1%), both measured 2026-09-20. The Racing Australia block that held thoroughbred SP at 0% when this was last measured on 2026-09-03 has lifted and the collector has been landing meetings since. A null `sp` is unknown, never zero — RA prints no SP at all on some rows. On placings, `sp` is copied from the matching `runners` entry when the response is built, so the two can never disagree. On a race with no `runners` payload the `sp` and `sp_note` KEYS ARE ABSENT from each placing — not present and null. The copy step is what creates them and it is skipped when there is nothing to copy from, so a schema-validating consumer sees a different object shape, not a null: read them with `.get()`. The keys are deliberately NOT normalised in, because adding them here would change the shipped payload of every COMPLETE race too, and nothing may move under a customer mid-integration. `field_status` tells you which case you are in before you look.

runners.title: Runners
runners.description: One entry per runner: {number, box, name, position, status, abnormal, margin, time_s, dead_heat}. Presence in this list is NOT proof the runner started. `status` is what says so, and `status` is what you settle on. ⚠️ COVERAGE. Read `field_status` on the row FIRST — it is the per-race answer, and it is what separates a field that has not been filled yet from one that never will be. Two different facts live here. (1) WHETHER THERE IS A FIELD AT ALL. Measured 2026-09-10 across the whole retained store — 5,577 results, 2,902 of them serving `runners: null`: AU greyhound carried a field on 2,360 of 3,219 races, AU thoroughbred on 315 of 1,104, and AU harness, NZ thoroughbred and NZ harness on none, as no collector covered those three codes then. Since 2026-10-04 TAB New Zealand fills them (`field_source: tabnz`, hourly, seven-day window) and has replaced the board copies described next wherever it could match the race; /v1/racing/results/coverage gives the current share per day, code and venue. FROM 2026-09-29 harness and NZ fields come from the pre-race board (origin: board): driver, trainer, barrier, form; positions only for placegetters; no times, SP or margins. Such a field is copied from the live board when the result is first written, before the board is purged 10 minutes after the jump, so a race whose result landed after the purge still has none. On these entries `"origin": "board"` is set on every entry, `box` holds the barrier (as on thoroughbred entries), `jockey` is the harness DRIVER, `weight_kg` and `form` are what the board showed, `status` is `scratched` for a runner the race's scratchings or `deductions` name and `ran` otherwise, and `position` is set for placegetters ONLY — a null `position` on an `origin: board` entry means 'not a placegetter, or not known', never 'did not finish'. Inside the two supported codes it is not a clean ramp either: each is filled by a scheduled pass, and where that pass cannot match a race with certainty it writes nothing rather than another race's field, so past the fill window 104 of 2,201 AU greyhound races (4.7%) and 44 of 288 AU thoroughbred races (15.3%) keep `runners: null` for good — `field_status: unavailable`, and polling them will not help. `runners` is JSON null in every one of these cases and has never once been an empty array (0 empty arrays in the whole store, measured the same day), so `runners is None` is a safe test and an empty field is not a shape you have to handle. (2) THE SHAPE OF A FIELD THAT IS PRESENT, which is where the 2026-09-08 date belongs. An AU thoroughbred field WRITTEN from 2026-09-08 carries every starter plus every runner Racing Australia printed as scratched; one written before that date carries STARTERS ONLY, because the collector dropped RA's scratched rows and a stored field is never rewritten. Measured 2026-09-08, all 244 thoroughbred fields stored at that point were the old shape and 198 of them publish a `deductions` row for a horse absent from `runners`. So on an older race `deductions` is the list of scratchings and `runners` is the starters; do not read a short `runners` array as a small field. Greyhound fields have carried the whole field since greyhound collection began on the 2026-08-21 Sydney card — but 859 AU greyhound races carry no field at all, which is question (1) and not this one. `position` is the finishing position for every runner that completed the race — not just the placegetters — and is null whenever there is none: the runner did not start, or it started and did not finish (except on an `origin: board` entry, which carries placegetters' positions only — see above). `status` is ran | scratched | late_scratching | reserve (an emergency that never got a start). `abnormal` is the official reason cell, passed through VERBATIM from the source — on AU thoroughbred it is Racing Australia's own Finish cell whenever that cell is not a number. THERE IS NO CLOSED LIST OF CODES and you should not write a match statement that assumes one: the source invents them, and a code nobody here has seen before will reach you unchanged rather than be dropped or renamed. Everything stored to date, with counts as at 2026-09-14: Fell (101), TailedOff (32), SB (25), PulledUp (8), FF (1, Rosehill R4 on 2026-09-12), LP (1). Treat `abnormal` as the authoritative explanation for a missing `position`, and treat an unfamiliar value as a did-not-finish unless `status` says otherwise — which is exactly what this API does: only codes PROVEN to mean the runner never left the barrier flip `status` to `scratched`, and that list currently holds one entry, 'SB'. Anything else stays `ran`, deliberately, because misreading a starter as a non-starter turns a losing bet into a refund. It carries TWO families that settle in OPPOSITE directions, so read it with `status` and never alone. (1) A DID-NOT-FINISH reason on a row whose `status` is `ran` — Fell, PulledUp, Disqualified, TailedOff, StayedInBox, FF and LP are the ones seen so far: the runner started and simply has no finishing position, and a bet on it lost. (2) A DID-NOT-START reason on a row whose `status` is `scratched` — 'SB', Racing Australia's code for scratched at the barrier: the runner was taken out of the market before the jump, so `position` is null, it is in no `placings` entry, and bets on it were refunded while the rest of the race was deducted. An 'SB' row may still carry `sp` — the last price Racing Australia printed for it, kept rather than blanked because it is a real market fact about the withdrawn runner. It is NOT the basis of the deduction, and you must never derive one from the other: `sp` comes from RA's results table while a deduction is struck by the settling bookmaker, and they do not agree. Measured 2026-09-08 across all five stored 'SB' rows that carry a price, 1/`sp` equals the published win deduction on NONE of them — Varejao, Sunshine Coast R4 2026-09-06, saddlecloth 5, withdrawn about 2 minutes 20 before the jump: `sp` 3.70, so 1/3.70 is 0.27 in the dollar, against a published `deductions` row of 0.18 win and 0.15 place; Dubai Dancer, Warrnambool R5: 1/5.50 is 0.18 against a published 0.10. Settle from `deductions`, which is authoritative. None of the five carries a `position` or a `margin`. Telling a barrier scratching from one made days earlier is CODE-SPECIFIC, and the two collectors do not spell it the same way — do not write one rule across categories. On AU thoroughbred (Racing Australia) both are `status: scratched`, and `abnormal` is the discriminator ONLY in one direction: a barrier scratching carries 'SB'; every other scratching carries `abnormal` null. Both carry their saddlecloth `number`, both carry `box` null (the runner has no barrier it jumped from — RA prints 0 there and we do not pass that sentinel on), and an ordinary scratching carries `sp` null while an 'SB' may carry one. So `abnormal == 'SB'` identifies a barrier scratching; `abnormal` null tells you only that it was not one, not how early it happened — use `deductions[].scratched_at` for that. On greyhound (our own collection since 2026-09-13: FastTrack for Victorian tracks to the 2026-10-13 card and PointsBet's settled race card from the 2026-10-14 card, the national results pages for every other state) `abnormal` is null on every scratching and `status` carries three values: `ran`, `scratched` (merged in from our own `deductions`, so it never says how late), and `reserve` for a rug 9/10 reserve that never got a box. `late_scratching` was the retired interim feed's greyhound-only value — a thoroughbred barrier scratching does NOT use it — and it is no longer emitted; `scratched` does not carry identical meaning in the two codes. `deductions` carries `scratched_at` for either, and is the one cross-code way to see how close to the jump a runner came out. `dead_heat` is true on each runner sharing a position. IDENTITY. `runner_ref` (`ra:<code>`) is the code Racing Australia published for this runner on race day. It is the same value on the closing-line, price-path and markets archives, on the live board on race day, and on /v1/racing/acceptances once that day's field has been read, so it joins this runner across every endpoint for this race. Racing Australia issues a new code for the same horse each day, so it is not a horse identity: the same horse carries a different `ra:` code at each meeting. `horse_ref` (`pe:<name>`) is: the registered name folded to letters and digits (trailing country parenthetical off), the same value on results, the live board, the closing-line and price-path archives, /v1/racing/horses/form, /v1/racing/horses/runs and the backfill, and it is the key to join a horse across meetings. It is derived at serve time from the name on the row, never stored, so every historical row carries it. On every racing code since 2026-10-16 — greyhound and harness runners carried a null before that and now carry the same `pe:<name>` fold, which for them is the only identity that joins a runner to itself across meetings. On GREYHOUNDS `runner_ref` IS the dog: `grv:<id>` for Victorian tracks as FastTrack numbers the dog and `grsa:<id>` elsewhere as the national results pages number it — per-dog registry ids that DO persist across meetings, in two namespaces, so a dog racing in both is two refs until mapped. `runner_ref` is null while a code's registry source is not yet wired. `trainer` and `jockey` come from the same official results source and may be null where that source is not yet live for the code. GREYHOUND-ONLY, ADDITIVE FROM 2026-09-21, five measured columns the results pages print. `first_split_s` is the first sectional in seconds exactly as the source page printed it, null where the page printed none. `second_split_s` is the second sectional, and is null on EVERY Victorian run because FastTrack publishes one split and not two. `weight_kg` is the greyhound's race-day weight in kilograms, null where the page carries no weight column at all — Western Australian meetings carry none (0 of 36 runner rows sampled 2026-09-21). `pir` is position-in-running text passed through as a STRING and never a number ("21" means 2nd at the first mark then 1st at the second): FastTrack's own column on Victorian runs and, since 2026-09-29, the national page's In Race Positions card elsewhere, which only some tracks print (see /v1/racing/greyhounds/form `pir` for the per-state rates) — the marks are each site's own, so compare PIR within one source; null where the page printed none. `weather` (added 2026-09-29) is the meeting's weather in the national page's OWN words ("Fine", "Light showers", "Overcast"), stamped on every entry of the field exactly as `grade` is; null on Victorian (FastTrack) fields, which print none, and ABSENT on fields written before it existed — measured 2026-09-29, 170 of the 2,012 stored greyhound fields carry it, from the 2026-09-27 card on. It is not on /v1/racing/greyhounds/form. `grade` is the race's grade in the SOURCE'S OWN WORDS — "M", "4/5" or "FFA" on the national pages, a race type such as "Tier 3 - Maiden" on FastTrack — and the two vocabularies are NOT mapped onto each other, so do not compare a Victorian grade with an interstate one. ⚠️ A STORED FIELD IS NEVER REWRITTEN, so a greyhound field written before 2026-09-21 carries none of these five keys AT ALL — absent, not null — and no thoroughbred field carries them in any era: read them with `.get()`. Measured on 46 freshly read race pages on 2026-09-21, a grade appeared on 46/46 races and 362/362 runner rows, a first split on 288/362 and a weight on 295/362; the rows without them are overwhelmingly rug 9/10 reserves, which never started and for which the page prints nothing. `sp` is the OFFICIAL STARTING PRICE as a decimal return on a $1 stake (4.6 means $4.60), null where it is unknown — never 0. It is the settling market's own price, not our consensus and not a bookmaker's fixed price: thoroughbred SP comes from the Racing Australia results table, greyhound SP from our own collection of published results (Victorian tracks via FastTrack, every other state via the national results pages, both from 2026-09-13), and HARNESS SP IS ALWAYS NULL — no source we hold publishes it. `sp_note` carries Racing Australia's favouritism marker on thoroughbred runners ('F' favourite, 'EF' equal favourite) and is null everywhere else. Coverage RE-MEASURED 2026-09-08 over the whole retained store, counting only rows whose `status` is `ran` (a barrier scratching is not a starter and its price is not in this denominator): 88.6% of thoroughbred starters carry `sp` (2,105 of 2,375); on the greyhound races collected since 2026-09-13, 2,054 of 2,077 Victorian starters do (98.9%) and 4233 of 4596 of the other states' starters do (92.1%), both measured 2026-09-20. The Racing Australia block that held thoroughbred SP at 0% when this was last measured on 2026-09-03 has lifted and the collector has been landing meetings since. A null `sp` is unknown, never zero — RA prints no SP at all on some rows. Null `runners` means the full field is not available for this race — never an empty field; every AU and NZ code carries one (AU thoroughbred, AU greyhound, AU harness, NZ harness, NZ thoroughbred). `placings` remains the source for the settling bookmaker's own fixed prices, and now also carries `sp` copied from here.

field_status.title: Field Status
field_status.description: Why `runners` is or is not there, per race — the field a caller was missing when `runners: null` was the only signal and it collapsed several different futures into one. SIX values. `complete`: `runners` is present. It is set whenever a field is stored, including on an abandoned race that unexpectedly carries one, so `field_status == 'complete'` is a safe gate before parsing. An AU harness result settled between 2026-09-29 and 2026-10-04 that the TAB New Zealand pass could not match may still hold the PRE-RACE BOARD copy — every entry `origin: board`, `field_source` null, positions for placegetters only and no times, SP or margins — so check `origin` before treating it like a collected field. On GB and IE thoroughbred (from 2026-10-06) `complete` means Betway's field (`field_source: betway_uk`, every entry `origin: betway_uk`): every runner with its starting price in `sp` and `sp_fraction` and a `position` wherever Betway publishes one — every finisher on the British races measured; on the Irish ones Betway ranks the first four first and the rest of the order within about 25 minutes of the off, which the interim result picks up, so until then an unplaced Irish starter is `ran` with `position` null — and non-runners as `scratched`; no margins, times, barriers, jockeys or dividends, and no Rule 4 figure on the deductions. On AU harness, NZ harness and NZ thoroughbred (from 2026-10-04) `complete` means the TAB New Zealand field (`field_source: tabnz`, every entry `origin: tabnz`): the full finishing order with margins in lengths, each runner's time (NZ racing only — TAB New Zealand publishes no times on Australian races), barrier and gate, driver in `jockey` (gallops add `weight_kg`, the total carried), trainer, scratchings with `scratched_at`, and TAB New Zealand's own pool win and place dividends on the placegetters; `sp` is null because TAB NZ publishes no official starting price. A board copy written before 2026-10-04 is replaced by the first pass. On ZA thoroughbred (from 2026-10-15) `complete` means the Ambernet settled race card (`field_source: easybet_za`; each entry's `origin` is the book it was read from, easybet_za or topbet_za): every runner, with a `position` on the runners the book ranks (the placed runners; unplaced starters stay `ran` with `position` null), jockey and trainer, non-runners as `scratched`; no margins, times, SP or dividends, and no deduction figure on the deductions. On US and Canadian racing (from 2026-08-01) `complete` means TVG's official results (`field_source: tvg`): the official finishing order, `number` = the betting interest (a coupled entry's runners share one) and `program` = the printed number, scratched runners as `scratched`, each runner's `jockey` (the driver on harness) and `trainer` as TVG prints them (surname first; archive cards filled 2026-10-27); no margins, times or SP — the tote dividends are on `dividends` (product US-TOTE) and per $1 on the placings. `pending`: a collector exists for this code and the pass that NORMALLY fills this race has not been yet; `field_note` names the UTC instant by which it will have run. `overdue`: that pass has been and gone without writing a field, but the collector still selects this row as a candidate and keeps re-attempting it — this state is NOT terminal. For AU greyhound the pass for its state (PointsBet's settled race card every 15 minutes for Victoria, the hourly national results pages elsewhere) re-reads every field-less race inside its seven-day window, and so does the hourly TAB New Zealand pass for AU harness, NZ harness and NZ thoroughbred; for AU thoroughbred a bounded re-fetch reaches six days but is run by hand rather than on a schedule. Most rows that reach `overdue` stay null, so do not build on a field arriving — but do not write the race off either, and `field_note` gives the horizon. `unavailable`: no scheduled pass still selects this row. Its collector's own candidate window closed at the instant in `field_note` and no field was written — the pass either never matched the race or refused an ambiguous match, which it does rather than write another race's field. `unsupported`: no collector exists for this category/country. Since 2026-10-04 that is only a foreign race that appears because an AU book listed the meeting: AU harness, NZ harness and NZ thoroughbred (1,254 of the 5,577 stored results on 2026-09-10) all gained their TAB New Zealand collector that day — and no amount of waiting will produce one. `not_applicable`: the race did not run (abandoned, postponed or transferred) and carries no field, so there is nothing to collect. TRANSITIONS, stated explicitly because acting on the wrong one costs you data. The scheduled progression is pending -> overdue -> unavailable, one direction only. It is bounded at every step by a collector's own window rather than by hope: a race can sit matched-and-never-resulted forever (The Gardens, 2026-09-05, 12 races), and an open-ended `pending` would have you polling it forever. Any of those three becomes `complete` the moment a field is written, AND THAT INCLUDES `unavailable` — nothing un-writes a `runners` array, so a collector re-run by hand, a widened window or a late upstream publication can still fill a row we have stopped scheduling passes for. So `unavailable` means 'nothing further is scheduled', never 'this can never arrive'; if you reconcile, re-read rather than caching it as final. `unsupported` and `not_applicable` are properties of the racing code and of the race itself, not of a schedule, and do not change on their own.

field_source.title: Field Source
field_source.description: Which collector owns `runners` for this race: `racing_australia` (AU thoroughbred), `fasttrack` (AU greyhound at Victorian tracks) and `grsa` (AU greyhound everywhere else), the last two our own collection, or null where no collector exists — including a `complete` AU harness row settled between 2026-09-29 and 2026-10-04 whose `runners` is still the pre-race board copy (`origin: board`), which no collector owns; `tabnz` (TAB New Zealand) owns AU harness, NZ harness and NZ thoroughbred; `betway_uk` (Betway's settlement feed) owns GB and IE thoroughbred from 2026-10-06; `pointsbetau` (PointsBet's settled race card) owns GB and IE greyhound from 2026-10-12. Set on `pending`, `overdue`, `unavailable` and `complete` rows alike — it names who WOULD fill the field, not who did — except on AU greyhound, where it names the source of the stored field once `complete`. `pointsbetau` (PointsBet's settled race card) owns Victorian greyhound races from the 2026-10-14 card and reads on any other AU greyhound row whose stored field came from that card (every entry `origin: pointsbetau`): finishing order as PointsBet ranks it, boxes, trainers and scratchings, with no times, splits, margins, weights, SP, PIR, grade or runner_ref. `fasttrack` owns Victorian races before that card.

field_note.title: Field Note
field_note.description: Prose for the non-`complete` states: which pass fills this code, when its normal pass for this race has been and gone, how long the collector keeps re-attempting the row, or that the code has no source at all. Null on `complete`, except an AU greyhound field from PointsBet's settled race card, where it says which parts that card carries. Written for a human reading a response — branch on `field_status`, never on this text.

completeness.title: Completeness
completeness.description: Added 2026-10-20, additive. Result and field completeness in one object, so a caller does not have to combine `status` and `field_status` itself. `state` is one of four values: `provisional` (the result is not final yet), `final_placings` (final placings, and dividends where the settling book declares them, but no full field — `field_status` says whether one is still coming), `complete_full_field` (final, and `runners` holds the whole field) and `not_run` (abandoned, postponed or transferred). `result_final` is `status == 'final'`; `result_source` names the feed that settled the race (`betright`, `pointsbetau`, `betway_uk`, `ambernet_za`, `racing_australia` for an abandonment, or null when unknown). For a race whose field is not in yet: `field_pending` / `field_overdue` mirror `field_status`, `field_due_by` is when the pass that normally fills it will have run, `overdue_since` is that same instant once it has passed, `retrying` is true while a scheduled pass still re-attempts the row and `retry_until` is the collector's retry horizon. `source_refused_since` (UTC) is set while the field's source is refusing our collector for this race (FastTrack, for Victorian greyhound races before the 2026-10-14 card; later Victorian races are collected from PointsBet's settled race card). `last_successful_collection_at` is the field collector's latest served run where the collector records one (FastTrack only; null for every other source). The four `state` values are counted per lane by /v1/racing/results/coverage (`result_completeness`). Read it with `.get()`.

availability.title: Availability
availability.description: Added 2026-10-22, additive. What this result holds, one part at a time, so a missing full field is never read as a missing result. `placings`: `final` (status final, placings present — settle on these), `provisional` (placings present, result not final yet), `pending` (no placings on the row yet) or `not_applicable` (the race did not run). `dividends`: `available` (at least one straight or exotic dividend in `dividends`), `pending` (none yet on a result that is not final), `not_published` (none, and none is coming: the settling feed publishes no dividends — GB and IE greyhounds, GB and IE thoroughbreds and South African thoroughbreds — or the final result declared none) or `not_applicable`. `full_field` (the whole finishing order in `runners`): `available`; `pending_collection` (a collector still re-attempts this race — `field_status` `pending` or `overdue`; poll no faster than hourly); `source_unavailable` (the only published source of this field is refusing our collector — today that can only be FastTrack, for Victorian greyhound races before the 2026-10-14 card (later ones are collected from PointsBet's settled race card); the date is `completeness.source_refused_since`, and `field_sources_refused` on the coverage endpoint lists every refusing source; the field fills on the next served pass if access returns, and placings and dividends are unaffected); `not_collected` (no scheduled pass still selects the race and none was written — `field_status` `unavailable`); `no_supported_source` (no full-field collector exists for this country and code — `field_status` `unsupported`); `not_applicable` (the race did not run). What a stored field contains per source is on `field_status`. Every value is counted per lane by /v1/racing/results/coverage (`availability`). New values may be added; treat an unknown one like `pending`. Read it with `.get()`.

deductions.title: Deductions
deductions.description: Scratched runners and the deduction applied to bets already struck. `win` and `place` are fractions of the dollar in the range 0-1 (0.34 = 34 cents in the dollar), as published by the settling bookmaker.

dividends.title: Dividends
dividends.description: Dividends declared for the race. `straight` holds one row per placegetter per product: {position, number, name, market ('WIN' or 'PLC'), product, amount}. `exotics` holds one row per exotic product: {type, code ('QN', 'EX', 'TF', 'FF'), selection, product, amount}, where `selection` is the winning saddlecloth numbers in finishing order, e.g. '5,1'. Every `amount` is the return on a $1 stake, the same convention as the odds fields — a 'FIXED' straight dividend equals that runner's own settled fixed price. `product` names the settling pool: 'FIXED' is the bookmaker's own price, the rest are tote products (SP, MIDDIV, VIC, RD+, BT+SP). A product that declared no dividend is omitted rather than returned as 0. Exotic dividends are only declared once the race fully settles, a few minutes after the placings, so a just-resulted race can carry `straight` while `exotics` is still empty — it fills in on a later poll. `multi_race` (from 2026-09-29) holds the meeting-level products — Quaddie, Giant 6, Daily Double and the like — on the race that is the product's FINAL leg and on no other race: one row per declared pool, {code (the book's own, e.g. 'RC-QUADDIE'), type ('Quaddie'), product ('VIC', 'BT', ...), selection (the winning saddlecloth in each leg, in leg order, e.g. '1,4,2,11'), amount (the return on $1), legs (the race numbers the product spans, e.g. [7, 8, 9, 10])}. Each row is published as the settling book declares it: Rosehill R10 on 2026-09-26 closed the Quaddie (R7-R10, $128.40 VIC and BT), a Giant 6 (R5-R10, $544.40 VIC) and a second Giant 6 row whose selection names five legs, at $1.00. A result stored before 2026-09-29 carries NO `multi_race` key at all — read it with `.get()` — and on a newer row it is a list, empty when the race closes no product. `straight_types` is the book's raw list of product codes, retained for backwards compatibility. `note` (rare, from 2026-10-03) is a plain-text caveat on the dividends, absent on almost every race: e.g. Randwick R1 on 2026-10-03, where the settling book paid on the first horse past the post and a protest then changed the official placings, so these dividends name a different winner from `placings`. Read it with `.get()`.

sectionals.title: Sectionals
sectionals.description: NSW harness sectional times, or null. Present on AU harness races at NSW tracks once Harness Racing NSW has published the meeting's Sectional Times sheet, usually a few days after the meeting, and it has been matched to this race by venue, Sydney date, race number and the winner's saddlecloth. Race level: `gross_time_s` (the winning time), `mile_rate_s`, `lead_time_s` (null where none was taken), `quarters_s` (the leader's four quarters, in order), `distance_m`. `runners` lists every starter by saddlecloth `number` with `name`, `position` (the official placing; dead heats share it and set `dead_heat`), `margin_m` (metres behind the winner), `time_s` (the runner's own time), `behind_800m_m` and `wide_800m`, `behind_400m_m` and `wide_400m` (metres behind the leader and how many horses wide, at the 800 m and the 400 m), and `q3_s` and `q4_s` (the runner's own third and fourth quarters). `source` is `hrnsw` and `source_url` is the sheet it was read from. Times are in seconds and distances in metres. Read it with `.get()`.

market_closed_at.title: Market Closed At
market_closed_at.description: UTC time at which the market was FIRST seen shut — the book stopped taking bets on this race. Poll-observed: this is the first poll that saw the state, not the exact instant, so it lands up to one polling pass after it, and passes are most frequent in the minutes before the jump. Set once: a market that flickers SUSPENDED -> OPEN -> SUSPENDED keeps the FIRST suspension. TWO SOURCES report market state. PointsBet closes its book at the real jump — measured 2026-09-03 over 9 live races followed across their jump, 0.2 to 1.4 minutes AFTER the advertised start on AU/NZ cards — and the Betfair Exchange reports it while it quotes the market, which is until about two minutes before the jump. `market_state_source` names the one that produced this value. Exchange-sourced stamps are withheld from customer plans, so a race seen shut only by the exchange reads null. Bookmaker-sourced stamps are served to everybody. Null also means no feed observed a transition — it never means the market stayed open. Copied from the live race row when the result is written; that row is deleted 10 minutes after the jump and results land a median 4.9 minutes after the start, so a late result keeps null.

inplay_at.title: Inplay At
inplay_at.description: UTC time at which the race was FIRST seen in-play — the actual off, as opposed to `start_time`, which is the ADVERTISED off and moves. Same poll-observed, set-once semantics as `market_closed_at`, and withheld on the same source rule. Reported by the Betfair Exchange only: bookmakers do not run racing in-play, so a bookmaker feed says when it CLOSED its book, not when the race went. For a race the exchange has stopped quoting, `market_closed_at` from a bookmaker is the closest measured instant to the off. Copied from the live race row when the result is written; that row is deleted 10 minutes after the jump and results land a median 4.9 minutes after the start, so a late result keeps null.

market_state_source.title: Market State Source
market_state_source.description: Which feed's market state produced `market_closed_at` / `inplay_at` on this race — 'pointsbetau' for the bookmaker, 'betfair_ex_au' for the exchange. Set once, alongside the first stamp. Null when no transition has been observed, and null for customer plans whenever the stamps themselves are withheld, so a non-null value here is always the provenance of values you can see.

race_id_aliases.title: Race Id Aliases
race_id_aliases.description: Other race_ids that identify this same race. When books disagreed about a race's venue spelling, card or start, it can have been listed under two race_ids; the price history (and /v1/racing/next-to-go while it was open) may carry either. Both keep working: this result is returned for `race_id=` with either id, and every alias is listed here. Empty for almost every race.

data_age_seconds.title: Data Age Seconds
data_age_seconds.description: Age in seconds of the OLDEST bookmaker quote behind this race.

refresh_tier.title: Refresh Tier
refresh_tier.description: Which refresh rule this race is on, and therefore what the race-level `stale` means. `live` = inside 3 hours of the jump: books re-price it on every 8-20s poll, and `stale` fires past 120 seconds. `card` = further out: books re-price it about every 15 minutes so a full day fits inside their rate limits, and `stale` fires past 1800 seconds. Every published quote carries ITS OWN `refresh_tier`, and it can be `card` on a `live` race: Betr's upstream rate-limits us, so that book stops re-pricing every poll 30 minutes before the jump rather than 3 hours (PlayUp, on a 6-requests-a-minute budget, at 6 minutes), and its quotes between there and 3 hours are refreshed every 5-15 minutes, published as `card`, and judged against 1800 seconds (since 2026-09-07; before that they were marked stale). A book's tier is never tighter than its race's. `age_seconds` is the TRUE age in every case — only the threshold changes.

server_time.title: Server Time
server_time.description: Send this back as `since` on your next poll. Deliberately set back 30 seconds from the server clock so no in-flight write is skipped — the feed is at-least-once, not exactly-once.

at.title: At
at.description: When the changed file was published (UTC).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: orphan_merge: the archive folded a duplicate race record onto the race that was run, which moved or removed rows in this period. regeneration: any other change, most often late results or late closing lines inside the three-night settle window.

rows_removed.title: Rows Removed
rows_removed.description: Rows in the earlier file and not in this one.

rows_changed.title: Rows Changed
rows_changed.description: Rows present in both whose values changed. Null where the dataset has no row key or the file was too large to diff; rows_removed and rows_added are then the net row delta.

rows_added.title: Rows Added
rows_added.description: Rows in this file and not in the earlier one.

sha256_before.title: Sha256 Before
sha256_before.description: csv sha256 of the file replaced.

sha256_after.title: Sha256 After
sha256_after.description: csv sha256 of the file that replaced it.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Row counts before and after, the diff method, and for orphan_merge the merges counted.

notes: Newest first. A restatement is recorded when a regenerated file's csv sha256 differs from the file it replaces.

days.title: Days
days.description: How many Sydney days the window spans, ending today.

to_day.title: To Day
to_day.description: Last Sydney date counted — today in Sydney, so it is a PART day and its races are mostly `pending`.

coverage_from.title: Coverage From
coverage_from.description: Start time of the earliest result retained anywhere in the store, the same value /v1/racing/results puts on every row. ONE GLOBAL VALUE: it is the oldest Australian card, and it is not when any other lane began — South African results, for instance, start months later. Read `results_floors` for the per-lane answer.

results_floors.title: Results Floors
results_floors.description: From when a RESULT exists at all, per country and category, MEASURED from the store rather than typed (2026-10-17): `country`, `category`, `from` (the date of the earliest stored result for that lane, the race's OWN date — so a Great Britain, Ireland or South Africa lane is named by its own card, not by the Sydney day it fell on; `from_day` and `to_day` above are Sydney days, which is a different question) and `results` (how many it holds). This is the figure to read before settling or scoring a lane. It is NOT `coverage_from`, which is one global value — the earliest result anywhere, currently an Australian card — and so says nothing about when a newer lane began. It is NOT `field_floors` either: that is when the FULL FIELD began, which can be later than the result. Australian thoroughbreds have results from 2026-08-15 and fields only from 2026-09-01, so neither value can be inferred from the other. A lane absent from this list has no result in the store at any date: races in it are priced and archived but cannot be settled here, which is true of every country outside Australia, New Zealand, Great Britain, Ireland and South Africa.

field_floors.title: Field Floors
field_floors.description: Machine-readable twin of `field_scope` (2026-10-15): one row per country and category that has a full-field collector — `country`, `category`, `field_source` (the machine value `field_source` carries on /v1/racing/results), `source_name` and `from` (the earliest Sydney card a stored field exists for, measured). Codes outside this list hold placegetters only.

races.title: Races
races.description: Every stored result in the window, all codes and all states. races == complete + pending + overdue + unavailable + unsupported + not_applicable, always.

pending.title: Pending
pending.description: A collector exists and the pass that normally fills the race has not been yet.

overdue.title: Overdue
overdue.description: That pass has been and gone with no field written, but the collector still re-attempts the row. NOT a terminal state — see `field_status` on /v1/racing/results for the horizons.

unavailable.title: Unavailable
unavailable.description: Past the collector's own retry horizon: no scheduled pass still selects the row.

unsupported.title: Unsupported
unsupported.description: No collector has ever existed for the code.

not_applicable.title: Not Applicable
not_applicable.description: The race did not run (abandoned, postponed or transferred) and has no field — nothing to collect, not a gap.

collectable.title: Collectable
collectable.description: races - unsupported - not_applicable: the races in this window that could carry a field at all. It is the denominator of `supported_complete_pct`, published so that a null percentage is readable as 0-of-0 rather than guessed at.

complete_pct.title: Complete Pct
complete_pct.description: complete / races as a percentage, across the whole window including codes that can never carry a field. NULL — not 0.0 — when `races` is 0. An empty window has no coverage figure, and 0.0 there is a fabricated number that reads as total failure: a `days=1` window called between Sydney midnight and the day's first result is empty on most days (the median first result of a Sydney day lands at 10:50 local), so this is an ordinary case and not a corner.

supported_complete_pct.title: Supported Complete Pct
supported_complete_pct.description: complete / collectable: the figure to read if you only care about the codes we collect fields for. The raw `complete_pct` is dragged down by stored races in codes that had no collector before 2026-10-04 (AU harness and both NZ codes, 1,254 rows as at 2026-09-10). An AU harness result still carrying the 2026-09-29..10-04 pre-race board copy (`origin: board`) counts as complete AND collectable here, so on such a window separate them with `by_category`. NULL — not 0.0 — when `collectable` is 0, which happens on an empty window or one holding only foreign races. If you alert on this figure, treat null as 'no data' and never as 'zero coverage'.

by_category.title: By Category
by_category.description: One row per country + category over the window: {country, category, field_source, races, complete, pending, overdue, unavailable, unsupported, not_applicable}, which sum to `races`, plus four keys added 2026-10-19 that are NOT part of that sum: `result_final` (races whose result is final — placings, and dividends where the book publishes them, are in; this is independent of the full field), `overdue_source_refused` (the part of `overdue` whose source is currently refusing our collector, see `field_sources_refused`), `oldest_overdue_age_h` (hours since the start of the oldest `overdue` race, null when none) and `refused_since` (UTC, set while this row's source refuses us). Since 2026-10-20 each row also carries `result_completeness` {provisional, final_placings, complete_full_field, not_run}, a separate partition that also sums to the row's `races`.

by_day.title: By Day
by_day.description: One row per Sydney day + country + category, newest first, with the same counts. This is the day-by-day answer to 'is yesterday finished yet'.

venues_incomplete.title: Venues Incomplete
venues_incomplete.description: Venue-days still missing a field in a code we DO collect: {day, venue, venue_id, category, country, settled} plus every counter above (races, complete, pending, overdue, unavailable, unsupported, not_applicable), which sum to `races` exactly. Ordered worst first: most `unavailable`, then the biggest outstanding shortfall, then oldest day. `settled` is true when nothing on that venue-day can still fill (no `pending`, no `overdue`) — that is the difference between a genuine terminal gap and a card simply still in progress, and without it a day mid-fill outranks a real one. A venue-day is listed when complete + not_applicable < races: an abandoned card has nothing to collect and is NOT a shortfall. A venue-day whose only gap is `unsupported` is deliberately absent — it would be most of the list and it is already counted above. Capped at 200 entries; `venues_incomplete_truncated` says when the cap bit.

field_scope.title: Field Scope
field_scope.description: Prose: which codes are collected, from when, and what the never-collected codes are.

archive_races_in_window.title: Archive Races In Window
archive_races_in_window.description: AU and NZ closing-line archive races that started in this window at least 3 hours ago.

archive_races_without_result.title: Archive Races Without Result
archive_races_without_result.description: Of archive_races_in_window, races with no result row at all: a price history with nothing to settle it against. Not counted in `races`, which counts stored results only.

archive_races_result_unlinked.title: Archive Races Result Unlinked
archive_races_result_unlinked.description: Of archive_races_without_result, races for which a result DOES exist but under a different race_id (matched on category, a start within two minutes and the venue's first word — 'Mt Gambier' = 'Mount Gambier'). A join on race_id misses them; a join on venue, date and start time finds them. The rest of archive_races_without_result have no result at all — typically a race abandoned after it was priced, or a meeting the results feed never published. Added 2026-10-19; null when not computed.

result_join.title: Result Join
result_join.description: How many priced races join to a stored result, over the same window and population as `archive_races_in_window`: `window` {from, to, min_age_hours, countries}; `eligible_priced_races`; and five counts that always sum to it -- `joined_by_race_id` (a result carries the race's own race_id), `joined_via_alias` (the race was listed under two race_ids and its result is reachable through the other one; /v1/racing/results?race_id= resolves either), `unjoined_with_candidate` (a result exists under another race_id and meets the matching rules, but is not linked yet), `held_for_review` (a result under another race_id is close but the evidence is ambiguous or weak, so it is never linked automatically) and `no_stored_result` (no result near the race at all: typically a race abandoned without an official notice, or one the results source never published). `join_rate_pct` = (joined_by_race_id + joined_via_alias) / eligible_priced_races, null when the window is empty. `by_cause` breaks the alias, candidate and review counts down by why the race had two ids; `definition` states each count in one line. Null when not computed. Matching rules: same racing code, country, venue and local meeting date, start within 10 minutes, AND the same race number or at least 80% of the result's runners in the priced field; venue and start time alone never link a race.

result_completeness.title: Result Completeness
result_completeness.description: Added 2026-10-20: the window's races by RESULT completeness — `provisional`, `final_placings`, `complete_full_field`, `not_run`, the `completeness.state` values on /v1/racing/results. A SECOND partition of the same races, alongside the field states: provisional + final_placings + complete_full_field + not_run == races, always, and every `by_category` and `by_day` row carries the same object summing to its own `races`. `complete_full_field` is final AND carrying a field, so it can be smaller than `complete` (which counts a field on any row).

field_sources_refused.title: Field Sources Refused
field_sources_refused.description: Full-field sources currently refusing our collector (2026-10-19): one row per source with `field_source`, `source_name`, `http_status`, `refused_since` (the first refused run of the current streak, UTC) and `checked_at` (the latest run). Races of that source whose fill fell inside the refusal stay `overdue` and then `unavailable` and say so in `field_note`; their placings and deductions are unaffected. Listed only while the window holds such a race (`availability.full_field.source_unavailable` > 0): Victorian greyhound races from the 2026-10-14 card are collected from PointsBet's settled race card, so FastTrack appears here only for a window reaching earlier races. Empty when no race in the window is held back.

availability.title: Availability
availability.description: Added 2026-10-22: the window's races counted by each part of `availability` on /v1/racing/results — `placings` {final, provisional, pending, not_applicable}, `dividends` {available, pending, not_published, not_applicable} and `full_field` {available, pending_collection, source_unavailable, not_collected, no_supported_source, not_applicable}. THREE MORE PARTITIONS of the same races: each part's values sum to `races`, always, and every `by_category`, `by_day` and `venues_incomplete` row carries the same object summing to its own `races`. They sit beside the field states and do not replace them: `full_field.available` == `complete`, and `pending_collection` + `source_unavailable` + `not_collected` == pending + overdue + unavailable. `full_field.source_unavailable` with `placings.final` is the count of races you can settle whose full finishing order is held back by a refusing source (see `field_sources_refused`).

example.field_scope: Full fields are collected for AU thoroughbred (Racing Australia, from the 2026-08-15 card, the first day of results) and AU greyhound (the national results pages from 2026-09-13; Victoria from PointsBet's settled race card), NZ harness (TAB New Zealand, from the 2026-09-30 Sydney card), NZ thoroughbred (TAB New Zealand, from the 2026-09-30 card) and AU harness (TAB New Zealand, from the 2026-09-27 card). No pass reaches back beyond its own floor.

payout_email.title: Payout Email
payout_email.description: Where a cash remittance should go, if it differs from the account email. Ignored for `credits`.

code.title: Code
code.description: Requested referral code, first call only. 3-24 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Ignored once a code has been issued — a code that changes is a dead link on somebody's blog.

runner_ref.title: Runner Ref
runner_ref.description: That horse's ra: code from that meeting. Racing Australia issues a new code each day, so to look the horse up here pass its name.

feed.title: Feed
feed.description: Where the data comes from: our own collection of published AU thoroughbred results (Racing Australia's results pages, read hourly by our results collector), flattened to one row per horse per race and refreshed hourly. Not Racing Australia's form page — that is /v1/racing/horses/form.

coverage_from.title: Coverage From
coverage_from.description: The first complete card in the store. A horse's record here starts here — it is not a career.

coverage_to.title: Coverage To
coverage_to.description: Sydney date of the latest race in the store.

collectors.title: Collectors
collectors.description: Which of our collectors can contribute a run. AU thoroughbred results come from one: the Racing Australia results pages.

refreshed_hourly.title: Refreshed Hourly
refreshed_hourly.description: The store is rebuilt from our own results at :59 each hour, after the results pass.

results.title: Results
results.description: Runners that cleared the filters, largest move first, each with its race header.

feed.title: Feed
feed.description: Where the data comes from: our own collection of published AU greyhound results, every state but Victoria via the national results pages (runner_ref grsa:), Victorian tracks via FastTrack to the 2026-10-13 card (runner_ref grv:) and via PointsBet's settled race card from the 2026-10-14 card (`source: pointsbetau`: position, box and trainer, with no registry ref, times, splits or SP). Runs on or after `results_from` are races we settled ourselves; earlier runs are the same pages read back by our history collector. Refreshed hourly. On a British or Irish race (/v1/racing/greyhounds/field, from 2026-10-12) `region` reads GB-IE and the runs are our own GB/IE results from PointsBet's settled race card, read live.

coverage_from.title: Coverage From
coverage_from.description: Sydney date of the OLDEST run in the store. A dog's record here starts here.

results_from.title: Results From
