results_from.description: Sydney date our own settled results begin. A run on or after it has `origin: results` and a `result_id` that joins to /v1/racing/results; an earlier one has `origin: history` and does not.

coverage_to.title: Coverage To
coverage_to.description: Sydney date of the latest race in the store.

collectors.title: Collectors
collectors.description: Which of our collectors can contribute a run: `fasttrack` = Victorian tracks to the 2026-10-13 card, `grsa` = every other state, `pointsbetau` = PointsBet's settled race card: Victorian tracks from the 2026-10-14 card and any AU race the national pages left empty.

refreshed_hourly.title: Refreshed Hourly
refreshed_hourly.description: The store is rebuilt from our results at :58 each hour, after both collectors have written.

competition.title: Competition
competition.description: The league's own name for the competition, verbatim ('Telstra Premiership', '2026 NAB AFLW Season').

home_team.title: Home Team
home_team.description: The LEAGUE's spelling, which is not always a bookmaker's: the NRL publishes nicknames ('Roosters'), and AFLW clubs carry no '(W)' suffix here. Read `event_id` to join to the fixture you have prices for.

home_score.title: Home Score
home_score.description: Null until the league calls the match final — never 0 for an unplayed or abandoned fixture. For AFL this is the total (20.12 -> 132); `detail` keeps goals and behinds, which the total cannot express.

status.title: Status
status.description: `final` once the league says so; otherwise the league's own word for the state ('upcoming', 'unconfirmed_teams'), carried through rather than mapped, so a postponed fixture is never read as a result.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: The code's own scoring and state as the league published it. AFL carries {goals, behinds, totalScore, superGoals} per side.

event_id.title: Event Id
event_id.description: The fixture in GET /v1/sports/{sport_key}/odds this result belongs to, or null when it could not be tied to one CONFIDENTLY. Null is common and is not a defect: we keep the whole league season, while the odds feed holds only the fixtures we currently price. A null also appears where two of our fixtures matched equally well, in which case nothing is guessed — see `match_note`.

match_note.title: Match Note
match_note.description: How the result reached its fixture: `exact` (both team names identical once normalised), `fuzzy` (matched through the same name-matching the odds feed uses to unify bookmakers), `no candidate fixture`, or `ambiguous: N ...` where two fixtures matched and neither was chosen.

label.title: Label
label.description: What this key is for — 'results worker', 'Jo's laptop'. Shown in the pool view and in your usage breakdown.

monthly_cap.title: Monthly Cap
monthly_cap.description: Optional. The most credits THIS key may spend per month, hard, inside the account's shared pool — between 1 and the plan's own monthly allowance. Omit it (or send null) and the key may spend the whole pool. Caps reset with the pool on the 1st.

api_key.title: Api Key
api_key.description: The team key. Shown ONCE; it is stored hashed and cannot be recovered — only revoked and re-minted.

allowance.title: Allowance
allowance.description: Keys this account may hold, primary included.

max_monthly_cap.title: Max Monthly Cap
max_monthly_cap.description: The largest cap this plan accepts — its own monthly allowance.

monthly_cap.title: Monthly Cap
monthly_cap.description: This key's hard per-month credit cap, or null for no cap.

key_credits_used.title: Key Credits Used
key_credits_used.description: Credits charged against this key's own counter this period. That is the number the cap is checked against; it stays 0 on an uncapped team key, whose spending is only ever charged to the pool row. Use period_credits for what an uncapped key has spent.

label.title: Label
label.description: New label for this key. Omit to leave it alone.

monthly_cap.title: Monthly Cap
monthly_cap.description: Optional. The most credits THIS key may spend per month, hard, inside the account's shared pool — between 1 and the plan's own monthly allowance. Omit it (or send null) and the key may spend the whole pool. Caps reset with the pool on the 1st. Send null to REMOVE an existing cap; omit the field entirely to leave the cap as it is.

TeamKeyPatchIn.title: TeamKeyPatchIn
TeamKeyPatchIn.description:
Both fields are optional; only the ones PRESENT in the body are written.

`monthly_cap: null` is meaningful (remove the cap) and must not read as "unchanged", so
the handler asks model_fields_set which keys the caller actually sent rather than
inferring intent from a None that pydantic would produce either way.

source_race_id.title: Source Race Id
source_race_id.description: TVG's race key, tvg_<track>_<date>_<n>; the same key /v1/racing/results files the result under.

race_id.title: Race Id
race_id.description: The priced race this is, as next-to-go and price-history name it; null while no bookmaker prices the race.

tote.title: Tote
tote.description: North American tote odds for this race, from TVG's public race board (US and Canadian thoroughbred, quarter horse and harness), or null. A tote is a pool, not a bookmaker, so it sits here and never in a runner's `bookmakers`, best_win or any bookmaker count. `runners[]` carries per betting interest `morning_line` (the track's line, set before betting) and `win_odds` (the host tote's current odds-to-1), each as TVG sends it ('5/2') and as a decimal price (`morning_line_decimal`, `win_decimal` = 1 + odds, so 5/2 is 3.5), plus `win_pool`, that runner's WIN pool money in USD. `win_odds` is null until the WIN pool opens (`pools_open`) and on a scratched runner. Pre-race the odds are an estimate of the win payoff: a tote pays what the pool pays when it closes. `status` is open, off or official; `final` marks the odds the race settled on (read once it is official). `read_at` is our read of TVG. Null on a race no TVG race links to, which is every race outside the US and Canada. Added 2026-10-27. RACE DETAILS (added the same day): `surface` (Dirt, Turf, Synthetic; after a course change, with `surface_changed_from` naming the one it left, so a race taken off the turf reads Dirt from Turf), `track_condition` (Fast, Firm, Sloppy, Good...; null where the track reports none, which is most harness cards) and `condition_changed_at` when it changed today; `pools`, every pool the track runs on the race with its money in USD ({code, name, amount}: WN win, EX exacta, TR trifecta, SU superfecta, DB daily double, P3/P4/P5 pick-N...); and on a scratched runner `scratch_reason` ('Veterinarian', 'Stewards', 'Trainer') and `scratched_at` from the track's change log. Probables and will-pays are on /v1/racing/tote?exotics=true. RUNNER CARD (added the same day): each runner also carries `jockey` (the driver on harness), `trainer`, `weight_lb`, `age`, `sex`, `sire`, `dam`, `dam_sire` and `medication` ('L' = Lasix), names as TVG prints them (surname first), null until the card is read (within minutes of the race reaching TVG's board); a coupled entry joins its horses' names with ' / ', leaves weight and age null and lists each horse in `horses`. RACE CARD (added the same day): `race_class` ('Maiden Claiming', 'Allowance', 'Stakes'; on harness the gait, 'Pace' or 'Trot'), `conditions` (TVG's race description verbatim, which on some harness cards also carries the track's selections), `purse` in `purse_currency` (the track's own: USD in the US, CAD in Canada), `claiming_price` (null on a race that is not a claimer) and `age_restriction` (TVG's code, '3U' = three-year-olds and up); null until the race's card is read.

history.title: History
history.description: How this race's tote odds moved, oldest first: one point per read in which the win odds or the WIN pool changed, from an hour before post until the race is official, the last point being the `final` read. Each point carries `read_at` (our read of TVG), `secs_to_post` (TVG's post time minus read_at; negative once the race is past post, as US races often go late), `status`, the race's `win_pool`, and per live betting interest `number`, `win_odds` (odds-to-1), `win_decimal` and its `win_pool`. Scratched runners are left out. Null unless history=true; empty for a race read before 2026-10-27 or whose pools never opened in the window. Added 2026-10-27.

exotics.title: Exotics
exotics.description: Probables and will-pays from the race's last read, or null (only with exotics=true; null while nothing was read: they are read from 20 minutes before post, every two minutes, and once more when the race is official). `probables[]`, one per pool: {code, name, min_wager, combos}, each combo [first, second, payout] where `payout` is what a `min_wager` stake would return if that combination won now (an exacta is [winner, runner-up, payout]; a daily double [this race's winner, next race's winner, payout]; second is null on a single-runner pool); a combination with no money on it is left out. `will_pays[]`, multi-race pools after a leg is run: {code, name, stake, legs_won (the winning numbers so far), payouts: [[number in the last leg, payout for `stake`]]}. A pari-mutuel estimate: the pool pays what it holds when it closes. `read_at` is our read. Added 2026-10-27.

coverage_from.title: Coverage From
coverage_from.description: The first meeting day (Australia/Sydney) this store holds anything for -- the earlier of the change log's first day and Racing Australia's meeting block's first day, computed from the tables on every call, never a constant. Any `date` from here up to three days ahead is served; an earlier one is a free 422 naming this same day. Null only if the store could not be read, and then the pre-2026-09-29 rule (7 days back) applies.

official_block_from.title: Official Block From
official_block_from.description: The first meeting day Racing Australia's own meeting block (the `racing_australia` values in `current`: rail, track type, penetrometer, the official rating) is held for. Earlier than this the change log alone answers: until 2026-09-29 the block was deleted three days after each meeting, so a day before this date is NOT one on which RA published nothing -- its block is simply gone. Computed like coverage_from.

state.title: State
state.description: `ok` when Racing Australia is answering form reads, `walled` when it is serving its bot-protection challenge to every fresh read and nothing can be collected.

walled_since.title: Walled Since
walled_since.description: UTC time of the first refusal in the current streak, null when `state` is `ok`. This is the field that tells you a stalled queue is hours old rather than minutes.

walled_hours.title: Walled Hours
walled_hours.description: How long the current streak has run, in hours, null when `state` is `ok`.

note.title: Note
note.description: One sentence saying what that means for this job, in plain words.

reset_at.title: Reset At
reset_at.description: When this key's credit counter was LAST set to zero, in UTC, written without an offset (read it as ending in Z). Despite the name this is the start of the current period, not the next reset; it equals period_start, which is the clearer field to use.

period_start.title: Period Start
period_start.description: Start of the current credit period, in UTC, written without an offset (read it as ending in Z). For a key created part-way through a month this is the moment the key was created; after that it is the monthly reset.

next_reset_at.title: Next Reset At
next_reset_at.description: 00:00 UTC on the 1st of next month, written without an offset (read it as ending in Z). Calculated, not stored: the reset job starts at that time and finishes a few seconds later, so a request in the first seconds of a month can still count against the old period.

url.title: Url
url.description: HTTPS endpoint that receives the POST, on port 443 or 8443. Plain http://, a host that does not resolve, and a host that resolves to a private, loopback, link-local or other non-public address are rejected with 422. At most 5 subscriptions per API key (409 beyond that).

events.title: Events
events.description: Events to subscribe to. Three events have live producers: `arb.opportunity` (a cross-book arb opened), `race.odds_open` and `race.result`. `race.odds_open`: the first bookmaker prices for a race just landed — fires once per race, so you can fetch the card on push instead of schedule-polling. Since the early-market lanes of 2026-09-01 it fires HOURS ahead, not minutes: measured over the 48h to 2026-09-03 11:00 UTC, the first price landed a median 10.1h before the jump on AU thoroughbreds, 5.3h on greyhounds, 6.8h on harness - typically overnight or early morning for the day's card, from one or two early books; the full board fills inside about an hour of the jump. `race.result` (from 2026-10-13): a race's result just went `final` — fires once per race, carrying the race (`race_id`, `result_id`, venue, race number, start, country, category), the placings ({position, name, number, horse_ref}), the `dividends` where the settling source declares them, and `source`. `race_id` is the id race.odds_open and /v1/racing/next-to-go carried for the race, and is null on the rare result we could not link to a priced race (10 of 2,038 final results in the 7 days to 2026-10-12); `result_id` is always set. A result goes final once its placings have been stable for 30 minutes, and the event follows within about five minutes of that: measured over the 3 days to 2026-10-12, results went final a median 36 minutes after the advertised start on AU and NZ races (p90 39), 38 on British and Irish thoroughbreds, and about 4 on British and Irish greyhounds, whose source publishes the result already final. It is the same row /v1/racing/results serves, so settle on it exactly as you would on that endpoint. `odds.change` is delivered solely by POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/test. `market.suspend` was withdrawn on 2026-10-13 — it never had a producer — and is now refused with 422.

min_edge_pct.title: Min Edge Pct
min_edge_pct.description: Only deliver arb.opportunity when the theoretical edge is at least this percentage. Omit for every opportunity.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: Only deliver events for these sports. Sport keys as returned by GET /v1/sports; racing events (arbs, race.odds_open and race.result) arrive as racing_horse, racing_greyhound or racing_harness. Omit for all sports.

status.title: Status
status.description: delivered (receiver answered 2xx) or failed (every attempt refused or the answer was final, see `error`). Rows written before 2026-09-03 read `pending`.

attempt_count.title: Attempt Count
attempt_count.description: POST attempts made for this row: at most 2, or at most 6 when the delivery queue is enabled.

requeued.title: Requeued
requeued.description: Events queued for re-delivery by this call.

probe_event_id.title: Probe Event Id
probe_event_id.description: The `odds.change` probe queued to confirm the endpoint answers.

previous_secret_expires_at.title: Previous Secret Expires At
previous_secret_expires_at.description: Until then every delivery is also signed with the previous secret.

label.title: Label
label.description: What this widget is for — 'homepage next-to-go', 'AFL page'. Shown in GET /v1/widgets.

config.title: Config
config.description: Theme, links, allowed_origins, defaults, title, show_updated and max_fills_per_hour. Every field is optional; the response carries the normalised document that is actually stored.

config.title: Config
config.description: FULL replacement after validation, not a merge — send the whole config back with your change in it, or omit the field to leave the stored one alone.

type.description: Stable URI identifying the error class.

detail.description: Explanation of this occurrence. A string for most errors; an array of field errors for 422; an object for 429.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description:
**Get a free key** at [puntersedge.online/api](https://puntersedge.online/api).

Paste your key in the **Authorize** dialog (lock icon, top right of Swagger UI) to try all endpoints live.

tags.name: Racing
tags.description: Racing endpoints for next-to-go races, race events, runners and bookmaker prices. Every country is served by default — pass country=AU (or AU,NZ; GB,IE for Britain and Ireland; ZA for South Africa) to filter. Britain, Ireland and South Africa carry smaller panels than Australia, and a race in any other country usually carries a single bookmaker; measured books per race: https://puntersedge.online/coverage-report.json. AU carries thoroughbred, harness and greyhound; NZ carries thoroughbred and harness — there are no New Zealand greyhounds in the feed.

tags.name: Best Odds
tags.description: Best available price per selection, bookmaker comparison and arbitrage indicators.

tags.name: Sports
tags.description: Sports catalogue and market odds endpoints for AFL, NRL, NBA, tennis, cricket, rugby and more. Racing is NOT here — horse, harness and greyhound live under the Racing tag at /v1/racing/next-to-go and /v1/racing/events. There is no racing sport_key.

tags.name: Arb & Value
tags.description: Sports arbitrage scanners and overlay/value price comparison. Everything under this tag is SPORTS-ONLY and takes a sport_key — there is no racing arb scanner here. For cross-book racing value use GET /v1/racing/best-odds under the Racing tag: a market_percentage under 100 means the best prices across the Australian bookmakers beat the field.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Authenticated usage, credit balance, connector health and developer key utilities. Subscribers manage billing here too — GET /v1/billing/portal returns a Stripe portal link for changing the card, pulling invoices or cancelling, authenticated by the API key itself, so there is no separate account to create. It costs no credits.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Subscribe to real-time events via HTTP webhook. Payloads are HMAC-SHA256 signed. Creating a subscription and sending a test fire require Plus, Business, Platform or Scale; a Standard or Starter key issued before 20 September 2026 keeps them, and legacy Pro and Growth keys qualify too. Free and Hobby get 403. Listing your own subscriptions, reading their delivery log and deleting them stay open on every plan, so a downgraded key can still see and stop a subscription it owns.

tags.name: Signup
tags.description: Developer signup and API key creation endpoints. POST /v1/signup needs no key: a free signup emails the person a verification link and the key is activated and shown when they click it, so an assistant can start the signup for someone but cannot finish it for them.
